The other ten letters have none on DECODE, but clerks' clear copies of all ten are in the digitised Fagel registers, Nationaal Archief 1.10.29 inv. 5186 (1757) and 5187 (1758), found by WAINUT (PR #65, 21 Oct 2026) after the reading; the Lyonet sets NA 1.01.50 inv. 221/223 are not digitised.

system.notes: Groups separated by dots. A group-frequency cosine first split the letters into codes A and B; they share their common values, so A and B are one code (the split reflects homophone habits). R1071, in a different code C, was split off to affry1757c on 14 Oct 2026.

On 23 Oct 2026 the cleartext images of the other seven records were opened: each holds its contemporary decipherment, and R93, R96-R99, R102 and R115 were read from them with the figures deciding where they differ.

system.summary: Polyphonic substitution: each digit 1-9 stands for two letters, 0 is a null, with four-digit X0Y0 and dotted two-digit nomenclator codes.
conditions.prior_solution.where: George Lasry's reconstructed key (24 Oct 2020) is attached to every record R93-R102 and R115; no plaintext was posted. Serrano, Correspondencia diplomatica (1914) prints Alessandrino's correspondence and may give some of these letters in clear; not checked (HathiTrust blocked).

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's 2020 reconstructed key was attached to every DECODE record R93-R102 and R115 before the attempt; it is polyphonic (each digit two letters, zero a null), so the text was chosen by a beam search scored with an Italian language model. On 22 Oct 2026 the contemporary decipherments of R94 (f. 45r), R95 (f. 58r) and R100 (under the cipher, f. 280r), on DECODE as cleartext images, were transcribed and aligned with the figures; they extended the key (9 = con, dotted 0 = z, 0^.0 = et, codes 1040 lettere, 3020 quando, 3060 -mente, 4020 come, 4040 Milano, 4080 et, 5070/6050 Imbasciatore, 6060 Inquisitione, 8090 havere), with which R101 was read on the figures. On 23 Oct 2026 the cleartext images of the other seven records were opened: each holds its contemporary decipherment, and R93, R96-R99, R102 and R115 were read from them with the figures deciding where they differ.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's 2020 reconstructed key was attached to every DECODE record R93-R102 and R115 before the attempt; it is polyphonic (each digit two letters, zero a null), so the text was chosen by a beam search scored with an Italian language model. title: Cardinal Pascual de Aragón to Pedro de Aragón (BNE Mss/2043), syllabic cipher S1, p. 0496: key partial by our protocol, read in part against the contemporary margin
system.summary: Mixed syllabic cipher (S1): 1-2 digit numbers for letters and syllables (13 e, 16 a, 25 que, 22 se, 21 pa, 26-30 sa..su, 31-35 ma..mu, 36-40 ta..tu), letter-shaped signs read with a shifted consonant (te = de, ga = la, po/go = no, pa = na, ca = ua), simple signs (a = n, + = s, x = r, ø = o, a+ = l, r = u, ue = h), a few 3-digit numbers (281 = V.E.) and nulls.

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; titles; places
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; titles; places
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; titles; places
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; titles; places
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

title: J. C. Smissaert (Raad der Aziatische Bezittingen) to C. J. Prediger at Batavia, 20 Nov 1800 (Nationaal Archief 2.01.27.02 inv. 209): key of the letter cipher rebuilt from the clear minute and validated
system.summary: Simple substitution of letters for Dutch: each letter is a column of two digits, a top digit 1-7 over a bottom digit 1-4 (a 7 x 4 grid, 28 cells; i/j share one). Only the sensitive words are enciphered; word division kept.
conditions.prior_solution.where: The clear minute of the same letter is filed with it (scans 0001, 0002 left, 0004), with the passages to encipher underlined; the archive's description names the encipherment ('overbrenging in cijfer'). So the content is existing. No key, edition or study found: nothing in this repository (catalogue.json and research/leads.json on main 1e974a24, targets, issue and PR search for Batavia, Smissaert, Prediger, 2.01.27.02, Aziatische; GitHub API, 9 Nov 2026); two web searches without result.
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol hashed before the clear was read, one held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents found the file in a sweep of the Nationaal Archief, transcribed, aligned, built the key, measured and read. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the clear minute of the same letter, filed with it, and validated once on a held-out passage. The content is the minute's (existing); the key and the identification of the pair are the contribution.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): 0.933 of characters vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.433 (margin 0.500), coverage 0.983. Not blind on the held-out words (their clear was glimpsed before the freeze, declared); the key is built by script from the learning part only. 54 = f added after the measurement.

title: Pfalzgraf Johann Casimir to Ludwig Camerarius, 1629 (BSB Clm 10382): key of the two-digit letter cipher rebuilt from the contemporary glosses and validated
system.summary: Letter cipher for German with homophones in blocks of three consecutive two-digit numbers (14-16 a, 17-19 g, 20-22 n, 23-25 t, 26-28 b, 29-31 h, 32-34 o, 35-37 u/v, 38-40 c, 41-43 i, 44-46 p, 47-49 w, 50-52 d, 53-55 k, 59-61 x, 62-64 e, 65-67 l, 68-70 r, 71-73 y, 74-76 f, 77-79 m, 80-82 s, 83-85 z); 86 and up are nulls; numbers run together, no word division. 1-13 and 56-58 not seen. Names are spelled; no nomenclator seen on the leaves read.
conditions.prior_solution.where: The contemporary interlinear glosses on the letters are a decipherment of the time, so the content is not new. No printed key or edition of these letters found: Halm 1874 p. 60 lists them without a cipher note; not on DECODE; nothing at Cryptiana (Tomokiyo) or in Lasry's lists; this repository has no target for Clm 10382, Johann Casimir or Kleeburg (checked by the GitHub API on origin/main c786648b, 5 Nov 2026). Not opened: F. H. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955; 2nd ed. 2013) and Stålhane 1934 (the 'Camerarius key' cited by Waldispühl and Kopal).
conditions.human_role: WAINUT found the cipher while paging Clm 10382; Daniel Bourdeau's leads review (batch b71) vetted it as lead 2187. Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. title: Pfalzgraf Johann Casimir to Ludwig Camerarius, 1629 (BSB Clm 10382): key of the two-digit letter cipher rebuilt from the contemporary glosses and validated
system.summary: Letter cipher for German with homophones in blocks of three consecutive two-digit numbers (14-16 a, 17-19 g, 20-22 n, 23-25 t, 26-28 b, 29-31 h, 32-34 o, 35-37 u/v, 38-40 c, 41-43 i, 44-46 p, 47-49 w, 50-52 d, 53-55 k, 59-61 x, 62-64 e, 65-67 l, 68-70 r, 71-73 y, 74-76 f, 77-79 m, 80-82 s, 83-85 z); 86 and up are nulls; numbers run together, no word division. 1-13 and 56-58 not seen. Names are spelled; no nomenclator seen on the leaves read.
conditions.prior_solution.where: The contemporary interlinear glosses on the letters are a decipherment of the time, so the content is not new. No printed key or edition of these letters found: Halm 1874 p. 60 lists them without a cipher note; not on DECODE; nothing at Cryptiana (Tomokiyo) or in Lasry's lists; this repository has no target for Clm 10382, Johann Casimir or Kleeburg (checked by the GitHub API on origin/main c786648b, 5 Nov 2026). Not opened: F. H. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955; 2nd ed. 2013) and Stålhane 1934 (the 'Camerarius key' cited by Waldispühl and Kopal).
conditions.human_role: WAINUT found the cipher while paging Clm 10382; Daniel Bourdeau's leads review (batch b71) vetted it as lead 2187. Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.

title: Caulaincourt to Napoleon, Congress of Châtillon, February-March 1814: the undeciphered letter of 25 Feb 1814 (AN AF/IV/1676 no. 131) and its keyed siblings nos. 130 and 170-171 (catalogue 534)
system.summary: Numeric nomenclator to about 1200, groups separated by dots, some underlined. Whole words (paix, que, les, pour, dans), syllables (Bassano = 952 959/663 395) and some letters; homophones for frequent words (que = 264, 669, 1191); nulls likely. The same key serves no. 130 (25 Feb) and no. 170 (6 Mar): about 33 of 48 numbers that carry a decipherer's word in both documents give the same word or stem. That no. 131 is in it too is presumed from its date.

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Jean-Loko consulted AF/IV/1676 on microfilm at the Archives nationales (Pierrefitte) on 7 Nov 2026 and photographed the reader screen; the transcriptions (two independent readings per cipher), their reconciliation and the key alignment were done with Claude Code.
outcome.method_basis: No. 131, the target, is not read. outcome.notes: R75 and R84 read here for the first time; R77, R78 and R82, the other three ciphertexts this target names, were already read by Lasry in 2020. 0.92 is the share of enciphered tokens given a value; the independent measure of accuracy is the 77.5% letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75. R75 (25 Sept 1632) argues that the Swedish victories make an accommodation easier but the union far harder, and presses the French court to see how dangerous that power's reach towards the Mediterranean is to France itself. R84 (18 Dec 1632), a month after Lutzen, turns on 'quella vittoria' and ends with the Roman fear that the consequences will hold France disunited and unable to help her allies. The transcriptions are DECODE's and were not re-checked against the images. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.914 of tokens get a value. fraction_coherent 0.775 = the letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75 (the only independent check). codes_open counts R75/R84 only (68 of 73 distinct elements met); dossier-wide 117 of 123. Second pass 5 Oct 2026: images re-transcribed, whole-letter decoding, 17 more element values (315 = S.E., Richelieu; 938 = Monsieur; 411 = V.S. ...): 0.914 -> 0.958 measured (R75 0.962, R84 0.953); interlinear agreement 0.828. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R75 and R84 relabelled decoded, not read (open nomenclator elements in nearly every line; 117 of 123 elements unread); class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; Lasry's key and the six new element values stand. 22-23 Oct 2026, re-read (b18): both letters have complete contemporary decipherments among the png attachments of their DECODE records (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), never opened before; transcribed and aligned with the decode, eight values adopted (88 = del, 33 = gli, 541 armi, 171 Regno, 473 mentre, 497 tutt-, 491 quell-, 104 Olandesi, not Svedesi); both read, grade A. R75 opens with Schomberg's victory (Castelnaudary), not the Swedish one; its danger is the Dutch; R84 is a December 1632 letter on Gustavus' death, the Valtellina peace and Monsieur's flight.

system.sibling_key: Lead, not measured: de Castille's cipher (Clair 369 f. 11, Tomokiyo 2016-) has the same build: letter homophones drawn as d, theta, H, eta, q, g, long s, a barred ff, a barred #, pi as a null, two-digit syllable codes in the 73-99 range (85 con, 88 de, 89 di) and digits with two dots for syllables. Cocquet uses 86 (x3) and 89, o with two dots, pi, theta, round d, H, eta, q, g, long s and a barred ff. Baugy and Du Maurier are figure ciphers; the Clair 372/373 anonymous keys use numeric word codes.

system.notes: System fields describe document A. Review 27 Oct 2026: the table is printed in MHH Diplomataria XXIII (1874) p. 740 ('A Harsányi és Balogh Máté által használt titkos írás kulcsa'): reciprocal, a=m b=i c=p d=u,f e=g f=v g=e h=l i=b k=x l=h m=a n=q o=y p=c q=n r=z s=t t=s u=d,f x=k y=o z=r v,w=f; all 12 letter values rebuilt from the 4 Aug crib agree. conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
outcome.method_basis: Polybius structure confirmed, then frequency and repeat tests against a control from the same book show the 196 cells do not behave like enciphered English; no plaintext was obtained.
outcome.notes: Concluded the encipherment was botched and there is no recoverable plaintext; heavy null insertion not excluded.

title: Deboli and Gołuchowski, St Petersburg 1786-1787 (AGAD Zbiór Popielów 3): 14 despatches in the older Polish code read in part with the key of the time ZbPop 444 (partial reading explained)
system.summary: One-part Polish code in shuffled letter blocks (key ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska', 8 Mar 1783): groups 1-1969 for letters, syllables, endings, words and names, signal group 2345, nulls from 1970; half-marked groups (136 1/2 = Nas).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; places; titles
conditions.prior_solution.where: The cabinet's clear texts of 1786-87 are in AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 (header index: a clear of the same date for 8 of the 14 pieces; none for p13, p21, p28, p33, g1, g3); not opened by the reading agent. No edition of 1786-87 (the IH PAN edition stops at 1782). Catalogue 416 open; no target on origin/main (GitHub API, 6 Nov 2026).
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the scans, set the rules (protocols hashed before each step, threshold fixed in advance, clears of the time kept unopened) and answered blind shape plates on single digits (shapes only). AI agents transcribed the key and the despatches, tested the key, read and summarised. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the readings.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method_basis: Read with the key of the time ZbPop 444, transcribed from its scans; the key was tested on 1788 pairs and failed our 0.90 threshold (0.837), so every piece is offered as a partial reading explained.
outcome.contribution: transcription; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered test of the key of the time on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed before the clears): read by sense 0.874, 0.874 and 0.837 on the held-out pair (0.864 overall), against shuffled-key controls with maxima 0.08-0.12 (computation still running); criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed at that threshold; 444 confirmed as the key of 1783-88.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words excluded), counted by script on reading/*.md: 7040 words, 5499 certain, 256 probable, 4 restored, 1281 unresolved = 5755/7036 = 81.8%; per piece 0.696-0.905.

system.summary: One-part Polish code in shuffled letter blocks (key ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska', 8 Mar 1783): groups 1-1969 for letters, syllables, endings, words and names, signal group 2345, nulls from 1970; half-marked groups (136 1/2 = Nas).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; places; titles
conditions.prior_solution.where: The cabinet's clear texts of 1786-87 are in AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 (header index: a clear of the same date for 8 of the 14 pieces; none for p13, p21, p28, p33, g1, g3); not opened by the reading agent. No edition of 1786-87 (the IH PAN edition stops at 1782). Catalogue 416 open; no target on origin/main (GitHub API, 6 Nov 2026).
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the scans, set the rules (protocols hashed before each step, threshold fixed in advance, clears of the time kept unopened) and answered blind shape plates on single digits (shapes only). AI agents transcribed the key and the despatches, tested the key, read and summarised. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the readings.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method_basis: Read with the key of the time ZbPop 444, transcribed from its scans; the key was tested on 1788 pairs and failed our 0.90 threshold (0.837), so every piece is offered as a partial reading explained.
outcome.contribution: transcription; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered test of the key of the time on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed before the clears): read by sense 0.874, 0.874 and 0.837 on the held-out pair (0.864 overall), against shuffled-key controls with maxima 0.08-0.12 (computation still running); criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed at that threshold; 444 confirmed as the key of 1783-88.

title: Deboli and Gołuchowski, St Petersburg 1786-1787 (AGAD Zbiór Popielów 3): 14 despatches in the older Polish code read in part with the key of the time ZbPop 444 (partial reading explained)
system.summary: One-part Polish code in shuffled letter blocks (key ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska', 8 Mar 1783): groups 1-1969 for letters, syllables, endings, words and names, signal group 2345, nulls from 1970; half-marked groups (136 1/2 = Nas).
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; places; titles
conditions.prior_solution.where: The cabinet's clear texts of 1786-87 are in AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 (header index: a clear of the same date for 8 of the 14 pieces; none for p13, p21, p28, p33, g1, g3); not opened by the reading agent. No edition of 1786-87 (the IH PAN edition stops at 1782). Catalogue 416 open; no target on origin/main (GitHub API, 6 Nov 2026).
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the scans, set the rules (protocols hashed before each step, threshold fixed in advance, clears of the time kept unopened) and answered blind shape plates on single digits (shapes only). AI agents transcribed the key and the despatches, tested the key, read and summarised. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the readings.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method_basis: Read with the key of the time ZbPop 444, transcribed from its scans; the key was tested on 1788 pairs and failed our 0.90 threshold (0.837), so every piece is offered as a partial reading explained.
outcome.contribution: transcription; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered test of the key of the time on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed before the clears): read by sense 0.874, 0.874 and 0.837 on the held-out pair (0.864 overall), against shuffled-key controls with maxima 0.08-0.12 (computation still running); criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed at that threshold; 444 confirmed as the key of 1783-88.

title: C.W. von Düben, St Petersburg, to N.P. Gyldenstolpe and Queen Lovisa Ulrika, 1764-1765: numeric cipher letters filed with clear drafts (Riksarkivet K 259; Unsolved Catalogue no. 450)
system.summary: Two numeric systems in the volume, separated by value profiles. A (6 Mar 1764, 15 Nov 1765, and letter 96 of early 1764): one-part syllabic nomenclator with homophones and nulls below 100, partial key key_c01 (217 groups, 197 with a value) rebuilt from letter 96 and its clear (PR #566, 14 Nov 2026). B ('Chiffer n:o 2': 5 Oct 1764, 31 Dec 1764): two-part syllabic nomenclator with homophones, key c04 rebuilt from the clears on 120 and 127-128. Groups 1-~760, dots, scribe's strokes, flat frequencies.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments of both system A letters (interlinear gloss of 15 Nov 1765, 124R-126; clear 102R-103R for 6 Mar 1764) and of both system B letters (120; 127-128).
conditions.human_role: Problem posed as a pasted catalogue brief (catalogue 450); no target-specific intervention. Additional contribution: Bryan Payne supplied URL, requested continuation and PR submission; Codex performed research/transcription; exact model variant not recorded.

outcome.notes: In progress: two systems. System A (6 Mar 1764; 15 Nov 1765): both letters were deciphered at the time (clear 102R-103R; complete interlinear gloss that runs ahead of the cipher); key_c01 (PR #566, built on letter 96 and its clear 97R-99L only) decodes both against those decipherments (0.545 vs controls max 0.061; 0.261 vs 0.043) and passes a held-out check on 101R (0.767 of known groups; permuted keys 0.224-0.254; no threshold declared beforehand); key partial. Method for these letters: read from existing decipherment; strict counts and translations made 14 Nov 2026 (6 Mar 1764: 622 words, 0.998; 15 Nov 1765: 610 words, 1.000; sysA_1616/). The cipher of 6 Mar 1764 after 103L.08 is not in the volume as far as checked; 100R is the end of letter 96. System B (Chiffer n:o 2): key rebuilt from the 5 Oct 1764 clear on 120 and passed a pre-registered held-out test (0.563 vs controls max 0.083, 12 Nov 2026); re-tested once on the 31 Dec 1764 letter against its contemporary clear on 127-128 (0.535 vs controls max 0.059, 13 Nov 2026) and completed from that clear (key c04, 1,236 of 1,247 groups, partial). Both system B letters are read through their period clears. Chiffer n:o 1, 15 June 1764 (108R-110R): key_c01 passed a pre-registered held-out test against its contemporary clear 109R-110L (0.383 vs controls max 0.057, 14 Nov 2026); read through that clear (337 of 342 word tokens sure, 98.5 %; 341 by the contributor's count with probable words; order of events by the contributor's record). Open: the other Chiffer n:o 1 letters (87-89, 90R-93L, 104R-105L, 105R-108L, 110R-111 with clear 116, 112-115) and their clears; inventory in dudout/system_a/INVENTORY_chiffer1.md. Additional contribution in payne2026/NOTES.md; the 1771 fragment decode does not change the target class.

doc.plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment on 102R-103R (archivist's note 'Hör till chiffermeddelandet "4.83.445.196.552" etc 6 mars 1764'). The earlier 'does not fit' verdict (fb.py) is withdrawn on 14 Nov 2026: key_c01 (PR #566, built on letter 96 only) decodes 101R as the first page of this clear (0.767 of known groups agree on 101R; whole letter 0.261 against controls max 0.043). The cipher on 101R-102L covers the clear from 102R.01 to 103L.08 'Il reitera a' (all 33 number lines placed in order with key_c01, 14 Nov 2026); 102L ends mid-sentence. The cipher of the rest (103L.08-103R.13, 304 of 622 words) is not in the volume as far as checked: 100R, the earlier candidate, is the end of letter 96 (sysA_1616/README.md). Strict count of the clear: 622 words, 1 doubtful, read share 0.998; translation in sysA_1616/reading_1764-03-06.md.
doc.transcription.source: IIIF full-size images A0073297_00101, _00102 cut into bands
doc.transcription.notes: Single pass, 49 groups marked ?; 20 scribe's strokes kept as |. Counts from wem.load_cipher (strokes, deletions and marks excluded); _check_profile --measure counts 697 tokens including the strokes.
system.sibling_key: Three key tables at images 218-220 (a Swedish key naming Senator Düben, Fersen, Ribbing, Horn; the 1770-71 crown prince travel cipher; a 'marque ###' key with Panin, Bestucheff, Solms). Their value ranges do not fit these letters.
system.notes: Image 219 is a later copy of the crown prince's key, printed in Svenska Akademiens Handlingar 29 p. 259 per the note on the sheet. Payne contribution resolves the citation: Schück I p.259 prints a 1771 letter, not the key itself; key219 matches its numeric fragments. Additional vocabulary key at 162–168. No May key validated.

title: C.W. von Düben, St Petersburg, to N.P. Gyldenstolpe and Queen Lovisa Ulrika, 1764-1765: numeric cipher letters filed with clear drafts (Riksarkivet K 259; Unsolved Catalogue no. 450)
system.summary: Two numeric systems in the volume, separated by value profiles. A (6 Mar 1764, 15 Nov 1765, and letter 96 of early 1764): one-part syllabic nomenclator with homophones and nulls below 100, partial key key_c01 (217 groups, 197 with a value) rebuilt from letter 96 and its clear (PR #566, 14 Nov 2026). B ('Chiffer n:o 2': 5 Oct 1764, 31 Dec 1764): two-part syllabic nomenclator with homophones, key c04 rebuilt from the clears on 120 and 127-128. Groups 1-~760, dots, scribe's strokes, flat frequencies.

system.summary: Two numeric systems in the volume, separated by value profiles. title: Commissary Adolf Ebers (Eberschildt) in Moscow, 1662-1666 (Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica 3/b/602): key of the two-digit German letter code rebuilt from the contemporary glosses and validated
system.summary: German letter substitution with homophones, two-digit groups 15-95 separated by dots, mixed with clear German; a few letters have two numbers (a 15/77, e 22/81, f 24/25, n 45/89, o 47/90, s 94/53, t 95/55) and doubled letters have their own numbers (ll 42, mm 44, ss 54). Arabic numerals are written in clear. 46 seen once, unresolved.
conditions.prior_solution.where: The German glosses written over the code runs at the time are a decipherment, on every page checked (ours: 81, 98R, 101, 102R, 103, 106, 108, 124, 133, 138, 143; Daniel Bourdeau's leads review n09 of 6 Nov 2026: 106, 108, 112, 114, 119, 121, 138, 140, 145, 160), so the content is not new. No printed key or edition found (leads review n09: nothing on DECODE, at Cryptiana or in Lasry's lists); no target, branch or PR for Ebers or R0003225 in this repository (GitHub API, 10 Nov 2026).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's Riksarkivet sweep found the volume and his leads review n09 (6 Nov 2026) vetted it as lead 2315 ('read': glossed throughout). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the contemporary interlinear decipherment (glosses) of images 106 and 108 and validated once on image 138. The content is the glosses' (existing); the key is the contribution.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol and key hashed before the held-out part was transcribed; one measurement on image 138 (160 groups, 165 decoded positions): 0.909 of characters vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.047 (mean 0.021), margin 0.862. Threshold fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30. Later additions 53 = s and 55 = t are derived after the measurement and not tested; 46 unresolved.

system.summary: Stager route cipher: words written in columns and copied by a route set by an indicator word, with printed code words (two per meaning, meanings filled in by hand for each issue) for names, places, punctuation and common words, and padding words at the end.

conditions.prior_solution.where: Earlier readings in the Official Records; selected addition: U1 OR I/33 p486, McPhail OR I/33 p559, Grant OR I/32 II p407. The U1 printed parallel was located after its No.2 reading; other prior texts were visible during exploratory collation. U2 body was already clear in volunteer transcription. No universal novelty claim. A later local source search also located McPhail in OR I/32 II p394; its print image was checked and differs from I/33 p559.

doc.route: War Department, Washington -> telegraph offices at Fort Monroe, St Louis, Chattanooga, Baltimore and Harpers Ferry
doc.plaintext.source: Contributed by WAINUT (27 Oct 2026). War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 32 pt. 2 pp. 244, 263-264 and vol. 33 pp. 488, 489, 497, 503, 518-519 print 9 of the 14 telegrams (T2, T4-T11) in clear (contemporary/mssEC19_p1-7_OR.txt); T1 and T3 not found there. Addition 12 Nov 2026: U1 also appears in OR I/33 p486 (print image checked).
doc.transcription.source: Decoding the Civil War volunteers (Zooniverse, 2016-17), text field of the Huntington Digital Library page records 8893-8899
doc.transcription.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (27 Oct 2026). Pages 1, 3 and 4 checked word for word against the page images (IIIF canvases 8893, 8895, 8896): no difference. Count includes the headings, addresses and check words (docs/_check_profile.py --measure); the route transposition is not yet applied in this ledger, code words stand among clear words. The preserved original file is not overwritten; addition_2026-11-12 carries corrected standalone U1/U2 extracts and an image-checked U3 extract. Its correction ledger supersedes the earlier no-difference statement for U1.
system.notes: The ledgers record the telegrams with the route already undone, so only the code layer is open. Entries counts the Book #1 vocabulary rows of copy mssEC 43 (key_book1_mssEC43.tsv). Each meaning has two code words (left and right printed word): homophones in that sense. Units: the ledger text is words (code words among clear words); length unit "mixed".

system.summary: English letter cipher on the 24-letter alphabet: base alphabet shifted 7 (cipher a = plain h), frequent plain letters with extra equivalents taken from the same alphabet shifted 8 and 10 (occasionally 11 and 20), so that several printed letters carry two or three values; persons written with signs (55 and other cuts) and figures.

No printed or modern reading of this cipher text found (HMC Salisbury IV, V, XIII, XIV; Birch, Memoirs 1754; Butler, The Edmondes Papers 1913; Tomokiyo, Cryptiana; DECODE). Of the other 90: 38 words are allowed by the tested key but take a value chosen by sense, 29 need a letter outside it (shift 20, shift 11 or a value added by hand), 6 are weak, 5 are unread letter runs and 12 are the undeciphered person signs and figures (55 twice, the m-sign twice, the ho- and oo-signs, 4s, 300 twice, 26 three times). title: Cardinal Luigi d'Este's cipher, 1584-85: BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 (April 1584) and four passages of Colbert 338 (pp. 513, 517-518 and 523), all read in part with Tomokiyo's key (strict: f. 271 85.0%, p. 517 87.9%, p. 518 80.6%, p. 513 83.0%, p. 523 73.0%)
system.summary: Cardinal d'Este's cipher (Tomokiyo): letters as symbols and figures with homophones (a = rho, epsilon, barred f, large looped rho; e = small s, 18, dumbbell...), nulls (M, Z) and code signs ([Roy], [le pape], [qui], [Monsieur], [faire], [pour]).
conditions.prior_solution.where: The key: S. Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, 'Cardinal d'Este's Cipher (1584-1586)' (henryiii.htm), built on BnF fr. 16041-16042; Colbert 338 not cited, no letter edited. The text of p. 523: no edition found; Favalli, CHMO 49/2 (2024), read, covers 1569-1580 and does not mention it; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435, 1559-1580) not read in full. Catalogue 1572 open on origin/main (GitHub API, e2315f8a, 5 Nov 2026). p. 517 (13 Nov 2026): no edition found; one web search on Poigny / Montmorency / Joyeuse / Clermont-de-Lodève 1584 found nothing printing this advice. pp. 513 and 518 (13 Nov 2026): p. 513's cipher block is deciphered in the margin by a contemporary hand (our reading agrees); no edition of either page found (three web searches: Luigi d'Este's letters to Henri III / Villeroy, Longlée, Desjardins' Négociations avec la Toscane - its tome IV prints the Florentine envoys' dispatches, not d'Este's French letters; not checked page by page). fr. 16041 f. 271 (14 Nov 2026): Tomokiyo cites only ff. 259 and 264 of fr. 16041 and prints no decipherment; nothing on fr. 16041-16042 in this repository; one web search on this letter (Montmorency, the pope's illness, April 1584) found no edition; three short contemporary interlinear glosses on the page. Contemporary decipherments in the same volume, Colbert 338: the margin of p. 513 (its own cipher block) and p. 515, a contemporary clear copy of the whole letter pp. 517-518, found at the integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026), after the reading; nothing in the contributor's files mentions p. 515, and it was used only to attest y.

K-C03.1 (K-C03 + one clerical fix) then passed a pre-registered test on a new document, BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 (M5 0.451 vs 0.077, bar 0.45: passed by 0.001 only, 14 Nov 2026). Catalogue 1572 open on origin/main (GitHub API, e2315f8a, 5 Nov 2026). p. 517 (13 Nov 2026): no edition found; one web search on Poigny / Montmorency / Joyeuse / Clermont-de-Lodève 1584 found nothing printing this advice. pp. 513 and 518 (13 Nov 2026): p. 513's cipher block is deciphered in the margin by a contemporary hand (our reading agrees); no edition of either page found (three web searches: Luigi d'Este's letters to Henri III / Villeroy, Longlée, Desjardins' Négociations avec la Toscane - its tome IV prints the Florentine envoys' dispatches, not d'Este's French letters; not checked page by page). fr. 16041 f. 271 (14 Nov 2026): Tomokiyo cites only ff. 259 and 264 of fr. 16041 and prints no decipherment; nothing on fr. 16041-16042 in this repository; one web search on this letter (Montmorency, the pope's illness, April 1584) found no edition; three short contemporary interlinear glosses on the page. Contemporary decipherments in the same volume, Colbert 338: the margin of p. 513 (its own cipher block) and p. 515, a contemporary clear copy of the whole letter pp. 517-518, found at the integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026), after the reading; nothing in the contributor's files mentions p. 515, and it was used only to attest y.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Satoshi Tomokiyo's published d'Este table, adjusted on glossed and already-read pages of the same volume (keys K-C01, K-C02); K-C02 passed a pre-registered held-out test on p. 517 (bar 0.45, lowered from 0.60 before the test, by the contributor's record); two signs (Venus sign, barred dumbbell) stay open, and the code word y, a sense-only value at first, is attested as Espagne by the p. 513 margin and the p. 515 clear copy since the check of PR #557. pp. 518 and 513 (after PR #546) read with K-C02 unchanged plus probable values for new shapes (key-p518-513.tsv); the pre-registered test of these values (K-C03) could not run (p. 513 too short). K-C03.1 (K-C03 + one clerical fix) then passed a pre-registered test on a new document, BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 (M5 0.451 vs 0.077, bar 0.45: passed by 0.001 only, 14 Nov 2026). Integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026): M5 0.451 on f. 271 re-implemented and reproduced (best control 0.08-0.11 across shuffling seeds, so the gap holds); the frozen files of the three pre-registrations are not in the repository, so the order of events is by the contributor's record. doc.plaintext.source: Not on the record or online. A readable text of this letter is in BAV Chigi L III 65 (Farnese's letters to Poggio): Pastor, Geschichte der Paepste V (1909) p. 472 n. 5, summarises its argument from there. Register copies of Farnese's letters to Poggio 1541-42 are in AAV Lettere di principi 14A, minutes in Naples, Archivio di Stato, Carte Farnesiane (Cardauns, NB I/7, 1912, pp. 435-439). None is digitised (DigiVatLib checked 6 Nov 2026); not seen.
doc.transcription.source: DECODE transcription by MEG, 19 June 2020 (decode/DOC_R91_D2341_2341.txt, git-ignored; parsed to r91_cipher.txt and ciphertext_decode.txt); image re-read of every cipher line by the project with dots, struck digits and corrosion holes (reread/64r.txt, 64v.txt, 65r.txt), then a key-guided check of the unread stretches (KEYCHECK notes)
doc.transcription.notes: 2,956 digits measured on DECODE's transcript (no dots recorded); the image re-read has 2,963 digit positions (digits the transcriber skipped at cancellations and holes added, struck digits dropped), 136 certain dots. Corrections counted: ~15 firm or probable digit corrections in the re-read plus 7 in the key-guided check; ~25 further alternatives marked '?'. Heavy bleed-through and iron-gall corrosion; holes at the right edge of 64r and the line ends of 65r; 64v.12-13 openings and 65r.15-18 illegible.
system.doubled_letters: mostly written once (steso, efeto, tuto); bb has a code (02)
system.sibling_key: Same chancery and dossier as IA-2 (DECODE R92, Klee's key), which is a different design; Meister key no. 1 (Montepulciano) fails.
system.notes: Corrections to Meister's print found on this letter: b/c = 02 (Meister's 'or' a misprint), s/z/et = 1, null = 11, ci = 24, co = 26 (26 not in Meister); 23 undetermined. Polyphony: 2 = l/p, 4 = n/m, 6 = r/t, 1 = s/z/et, 01 = d/f/g, 02 = b/c/bb.

title: Charles V and Prince Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, 1546-1553 (Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554, Estense Modena; catalogue 1560 and 1561): two independent readings
system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary: slip c.29 (13 May), c.77 (23 Dec), the clerk's margin notes on c.64v (20 Nov) and c.50r (30 Sep). No decipherment of the 14 Nov letter was found. Bertomeu Masia 2009 studies the Parma and Piacenza cipher correspondence and was not seen; it may print some of these letters. WAINUT's search (3 Nov 2026): Calendar of State Papers Spain IX and Venice V and the Treccani DBI do not print the 14 Nov letter; Corpus documental de Carlos V vol. III, Druffel and the Simancas minutes not opened.

conditions.human_role: Gave the lead 1560 page, said 'solve that cipher', approved each continuation, then said to continue as far as possible and publish. No hints about the key or the content.

outcome.method_basis: The letters were matched to the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 and to Bertomeu Masia's reconstruction as pictured by Tomokiyo on Cryptiana. Its rule and sign table, extended from the text by hand, gave the 14 Nov letter, which has no decipherment. Folded in on 14 Nov 2026: WAINUT recovered a table for the same cipher apart, from the contemporary decipherments of Prince Philip's letters (c. 14r for c. 12r, c. 11 for cc. 9r-9v), froze it and read the 14 Nov letter with it (outcome.parts).

outcome.notes: Read by eye with the sense in view; values were chosen knowing what would make Spanish, so the readings are not a controlled test. The validation tests that a fitted key on shuffled text does worse; it does not check single words. No person has checked a passage against the image. Since 14 Nov 2026 the entry holds two readings made apart (the project's and WAINUT's); their comparison is the first cross-check either has had, and it was done on the files, not on the images.

system.notes: distinct_symbols counts sign names given here, some of which are variants of one sign. The key image was read at low resolution and extended from the text by hand. Clear words in the cipher: Pollo (the Pope, inferred), mus/mms (para, by sense), inta, em, vela/bela, nerp, gien, et ud, tu; not explained by the key. Folded in on 14 Nov 2026: WAINUT's table (wainut/key.tsv, 160 rows, its own sign names; wainut/key_frozen_1547.tsv frozen before the Charles letters) with the code words dide Su Magestad, quod Embaxador, gaces Rey de Francia, em franceses, gien vuestra, mus para from the contemporary decipherments of Philip's letters. Code values settled on 14 Nov 2026: Pollo Papa, mus/mms para, inta Su Santidad, em Franceses, gien vuestra, saa Duque, nerp/nep Francia (sense; the letters of the code word are open). Open: vela/bela, et ud, tu.

title: Charles V and Prince Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, 1546-1553 (Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554, Estense Modena; catalogue 1560 and 1561): two independent readings
system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary: slip c.29 (13 May), c.77 (23 Dec), the clerk's margin notes on c.64v (20 Nov) and c.50r (30 Sep). No decipherment of the 14 Nov letter was found. Bertomeu Masia 2009 studies the Parma and Piacenza cipher correspondence and was not seen; it may print some of these letters. WAINUT's search (3 Nov 2026): Calendar of State Papers Spain IX and Venice V and the Treccani DBI do not print the 14 Nov letter; Corpus documental de Carlos V vol. III, Druffel and the Simancas minutes not opened.

outcome.method_basis: The letters were matched to the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 and to Bertomeu Masia's reconstruction as pictured by Tomokiyo on Cryptiana. Folded in on 14 Nov 2026: WAINUT recovered a table for the same cipher apart, from the contemporary decipherments of Prince Philip's letters (c. 14r for c. 12r, c. 11 for cc. 9r-9v), froze it and read the 14 Nov letter with it (outcome.parts).

title: Charles V and Prince Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, 1546-1553 (Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554, Estense Modena; catalogue 1560 and 1561): two independent readings
system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary: slip c.29 (13 May), c.77 (23 Dec), the clerk's margin notes on c.64v (20 Nov) and c.50r (30 Sep). No decipherment of the 14 Nov letter was found. Bertomeu Masia 2009 studies the Parma and Piacenza cipher correspondence and was not seen; it may print some of these letters. WAINUT's search (3 Nov 2026): Calendar of State Papers Spain IX and Venice V and the Treccani DBI do not print the 14 Nov letter; Corpus documental de Carlos V vol. III, Druffel and the Simancas minutes not opened.

outcome.method_basis: The letters were matched to the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 and to Bertomeu Masia's reconstruction as pictured by Tomokiyo on Cryptiana. Its rule and sign table, extended from the text by hand, gave the 14 Nov letter, which has no decipherment. Folded in on 14 Nov 2026: WAINUT recovered a table for the same cipher apart, from the contemporary decipherments of Prince Philip's letters (c. 14r for c. 12r, c. 11 for cc. 9r-9v), froze it and read the 14 Nov letter with it (outcome.parts).

system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.

title: Charles V and Prince Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, 1546-1553 (Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554, Estense Modena; catalogue 1560 and 1561): two independent readings
system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.

system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.

system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.

Open: vela/bela, et ud, tu.

title: Charles V and Prince Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, 1546-1553 (Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554, Estense Modena; catalogue 1560 and 1561): two independent readings
system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary: slip c.29 (13 May), c.77 (23 Dec), the clerk's margin notes on c.64v (20 Nov) and c.50r (30 Sep). No decipherment of the 14 Nov letter was found. Bertomeu Masia 2009 studies the Parma and Piacenza cipher correspondence and was not seen; it may print some of these letters. WAINUT's search (3 Nov 2026): Calendar of State Papers Spain IX and Venice V and the Treccani DBI do not print the 14 Nov letter; Corpus documental de Carlos V vol. III, Druffel and the Simancas minutes not opened.

system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.

system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).

system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).

system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).

system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).

system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).

title: David Humphreys to Pickering, Madrid, 1799: the coded parts of despatches Nos. 188 and 214, read with his code rebuilt from the State Department's decipherments
system.summary: One-part scrambled numerical code of about 1,600 elements (numbers 2-1590 seen) for words, syllables, single letters and punctuation, with a few homophones: Jefferson's 'Code No. 8' of 1785 (Boyd), Weber's unlocated '994 = the' code.
conditions.prior_solution.where: For Nos. 188 and 214 none found: no decipherment on or after either copy on the film, no second copy on M31 rolls 5-7, and no print (Naval Documents, Quasi-War vols. 2 and 4; American State Papers, Foreign Relations vol. 2; Pickering Papers calendar; F. L. Humphreys 1917). Whether the Department deciphered the copies it received first is not established. The code itself: the State Department's clerks deciphered other despatches in it (our crib); the Papers of Thomas Jefferson decoded the 1791 letters with a partially reconstructed Code No. 8 (communication from James P. McClure, 2012, unpublished); F. L. Humphreys (1917) printed the 1791 letters decoded by 'Dr. Lowndes'; the Madison Papers print Jacob Wagner's decodings of March 1801.

title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski to Pál Ráday, enciphering drafts 1705 and 1706-07 (SBB Berlin, Nachl. Francke 11,2/15 and 11,2/16): key of the numeric syllabary rebuilt from the drafts and validated on a held-out draft
system.summary: One-part numeric syllabary in alphabetical order: single letters with homophones (30-70 and round numbers 110-300), syllables in alphabetical order (84 ab ... 223 ut), a few code words (225 imperator/Caesar, 226 Hungaria, 227 Prussia, 228 Polonia, 229 Suecia, 231 Anglia, 232/237 Gallia, 233 Hispania, 234 Italia, 236 Elector, 241 Rex), nulls below 30 and 301-310, 390, 401. Groups separated by dots. Same system in 1705 and 1706-07.
conditions.prior_solution.where: The drafts carry Jablonski's own Latin under the numbers (Daniel Bourdeau's leads review c26, 4 Nov 2026: leads 2169/2170 'read', key not built). The received letter of 3 Aug 1705 (glossed by Ráday) is reproduced in Révay Zoltán, II. Rákóczi Ferenc és korának rejtjelezése (Budapest, MNHF, 1974; Wikimedia Commons scan); whether Révay prints the key could not be checked (no open text found, 10 Nov 2026). Benda, Levéltári Közlemények 25 (1954) cites a clavis for the Jablonski correspondence in the Ráday archive (not seen). No target, branch or PR on these drafts in this repository; R483 (rakoczi1711) is another system.
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's SBB/Kalliope sweep found the drafts (leads 2168-2171) and his leads review c26 (4 Nov 2026) vetted them as 'read' (enciphering drafts). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the Latin written under the numbers in Jablonski's enciphering drafts (11,2/15 nos 8, 13, 33; 11,2/16 no 42) and validated once on a held-out draft (11,2/16 no 44). The content is the drafts' own (existing); the key is the contribution.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol (frozen/01_PREREG.md) and key (frozen/03_KEY.json) hashed before the held-out draft 11,2/16 no 44 (scans 91-92) was transcribed; 541 groups transcribed blind; one measurement: 0.930 of characters (958 decoded / 952 reference letters) vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.247 (mean 0.198), margin 0.683. Thresholds fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30. The script also folds w->u, y->i (not named in the protocol; declared). Key not changed after the measurement.

title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)
system.summary: A two-part numerical code of about 1,750 groups (words, syllables, letters, punctuation), groups separated by dots, with homophones.

outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.

This is an estimate: fragments of words in the files make the word count approximate. The 1,868 of 1,917 counted groups (0.974) of reading.tsv are a count of groups, and the Adams postscript (about 30 groups, blotted) is outside both. Before: 0.974 (groups).

title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)
system.summary: A two-part numerical code of about 1,750 groups (words, syllables, letters, punctuation), groups separated by dots, with homophones.

outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.

This is an estimate: fragments of words in the files make the word count approximate. The 1,868 of 1,917 counted groups (0.974) of reading.tsv are a count of groups, and the Adams postscript (about 30 groups, blotted) is outside both. Before: 0.974 (groups).

title: Kanawha district route-cipher telegrams, West Virginia, 1-3 July 1863 (Gilder Lehrman GLC02414): route and code words recovered from the decipherments of the time, a held-out test passed, and the one undeciphered telegram read in part
system.summary: Union military-telegraph route cipher: words written six to a row under a heading row, taken off up column 5, down 1, up 4, down 2, up 6, down 3; a commencement word gives the number of rows; local code words for places, names and military terms.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the research direction and the posting restraint and opened the library subscription in his browser; AI agents transcribed, recovered the route and code words, froze the keys, ran both tests and packaged the folder. No human reading check.
outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The route and the code words were recovered by matching the cipher telegrams with decipherments of the time kept as separate items in the same collection (.114, .137, .138); the frozen key then predicted a held-out decipherment (.185, 60 of 66 cells) and was applied to .339, which has none.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; sender or date identified
outcome.validation.notes: Route transposition of whole words with a code layer: the character-level test has no token alignment to score. The key was instead tested on a held-out decipherment written before scoring (freeze/round2: 60 of 66 cells; 200 random routes, maximum 40).
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; matched control; statistical test

outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

title: Lope Hurtado de Mendoza (Rome) to Charles V, May 1523 - Mar 1524 - RAH Salazar 9/28 and 9/30, DECODE R9667-R9869
system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.

title: Lope Hurtado de Mendoza (Rome) to Charles V, May 1523 - Mar 1524 - RAH Salazar 9/28 and 9/30, DECODE R9667-R9869
system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.

That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

Found by Michael Brackx (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026); checked on the images here the same day. Transcribed by him (AI-assisted, unchecked by a second person).
doc.transcription.source: Michael Brackx (issues #73, #77-#79, #83), from full-size deskewed line crops (openapi.bnf.fr), AI-assisted (Claude Code), unchecked by a second person; brackx2026/
doc.transcription.notes: Re-transcribed by Brackx, 21 lines. Measured 22 Oct 2026 (brackx_validate.py, this project's decoder over his per-leaf key): 70% of tokens read as sense. Earlier transcription kept: 21 cipher lines after a clear first half; three passes; about two thirds read (f143_reading.md). Measured (measure.py, 22 Sept 2026): 59% of transcribed tokens read as sense (424/724); scrambled-key floor 11%, chance-corrected 54%; 21/21 lines transcribed.
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Maximilian I's envoys in cipher, 1510-1512: de Burgo, de Laude, Veit von Fürst, Gattinara, Colla (HHStA RK Maximiliana; Unsolved Catalogue 495)
system.summary: Four systems. De Burgo's (also used by de Laude): one sign per letter, 2-3 homophones for common letters, many vowels dropped, word signs (ro = et, g t 4 a ŧ o = quod, 93 = Cesar/Maiestas Vestra, ⊞ = pro). Fürst: glyph-letter substitution for single words inside clear Latin, plus sign-names. Gattinara: digit/symbol letters, homophones, name signs (struck x c + o = Maiestas, S°p° = principis Caroli). Colla and Modena: own alphabets, not analysed.
