title: Undated cipher letter, probably to Lorenzo de' Medici (ASF Mediceo avanti il Principato XLVIII 214r, catalogue 2309): the Siena no. 11 cipher identified, read in part with George Lasry's key (partial; partial reading explained)
system.summary: The Siena no. 11 cipher (Florentine, Medici chancery): homophonic substitution with invented signs, letters and numerals, the same nulls 'g#', '31' and '87'; 52 sign types in 2309, 14 of them (3.6 % of the tokens) not in George Lasry's key; one of them, TRI (a triangle), held as 'che' on a fresh portion on 12 Nov 2026, which leaves 13 (2.8 %).
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment on the leaf or in the inventory; web search of 10 Nov 2026 found nothing on MAP XLVIII 214; Marco Vito's work concerns letters of 1486-1491; catalogue 2309 open, no target for it on origin/main.
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (each step pre-registered and hashed, thresholds fixed in advance, one measurement per test). AI agents compared the sign set with the known keys, transcribed, measured and read. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the reading.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The sign set of 2309 matches Siena no. 11; George Lasry's key of that letter (targets/siena11) was applied unchanged, plus two single values derived later and held on a fresh portion (D1 'PLUS ODAG' = c, TRI = che). The key failed a test on 2309 itself and is partial on two held-out portions of a letter of the same family (XLVIII 294 against its clear c. 276).
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests (not docs/_validate.py). On 2309 itself: M5 0.2335 vs at most 0.0719 for 200 shuffled keys, margin 0.16 under 0.30: not met (failed). Held out on XLVIII 294 c. 306v against its contemporary clear c. 276: 0.6419 vs at most 0.2045, margin 0.437, under the 0.85 set in advance: partial. Third test 12 Nov 2026 on c. 306r (fresh) against c. 276r: 0.6519 vs at most 0.1854, partial; D1 ('PLUS ODAG' = c) held 5/6 and TRI = che 4/5 (p = 0.005 each, 200 random-position controls).
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading/xlviii214.md (12 Nov 2026): certain + probable words cover about 35 % of the 683 decoded letters, about 45 % with the restored words (10 Nov: 33 % and 43 % of 665); stated as about 35-45 %.

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test

Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

title: Cosimo III's autograph letter cipher to his envoy Montauti (Penn Ms. Codex 533), key rebuilt from the interlined secretariat despatches of Codex 534, 1690-1694
system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.
conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.
outcome.validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent verification; statistical test

title: Duplessis-Mornay correspondents 1593-1597: undeciphered figures printed in the 1824 Mémoires et correspondance
system.summary: Numeric groups of 2-4 digits separated by full stops, set inside clear letters. Most groups split into two numbers of 2-24 (2210 = 22|10, 912 = 9|12); the editors of 1824 printed them as figures because they had no key.

The other Rohan 1597 groups that take a value are letters of names that read only with the inferred values 672, 134, 160, 38 (R2, R7, R19), the word-code half of 'le [672]' (R5, R8), or single figures that Beling's own table says are name codes (R3, R4, R6, R11, R14, R16, R17, R18). title: Cardinal Morosini, nuncio and legate in France, to Rome, 1587-89: 35 cipher enclosures in Meister's key no. 40 (AAV Segr. Stato Francia 22, DECODE R18-R22, R27-R49, R51, R52, R55-R58; Francia 18/3, DECODE R17)
system.summary: Meister no. 40 (1587): homophonic letters, clusters and common words in 1-3 digit figures run together without separators, three-digit dotted nomenclator, nulls 8x.
system.nomenclator.kinds: syllables; common words; names; places; titles
conditions.prior_solution.where: Key printed in Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie (1906) no. 40; Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18 (DOC_3175, Oct 2020) with the note 'full key in Meister'; no plaintext posted, records listed 'partially decrypted'. R17's DECODE note names the same Meister key; its decryption file is a Java error trace. Found 22 Oct 2026, after the readings: Rome deciphered these letters at the time (ASV Segr. Stato Francia 27, cited by Hübner 1870, not imaged), and Tempesti 1754 paraphrases parts of many of them.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code and posed the problem; no target-specific intervention recorded.
outcome.method_basis: Meister 1906 no. 40, the key printed for Morosini's nunciature (Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18), applied to DECODE's volunteer transcriptions. The character decode left garbled words in most lines; on 22 Oct 2026 a word-level decoder with a transcription-slip model and a hand re-parse of every break on the figures (and on the images where a figure was in doubt) turned 34 of the 35 enclosures into sentences, translated; most garbles were spurious nomenclator dots in the transcriptions and the clerk's -mente abbreviation (m + null 8). R35, a Spanish copy, still has too many holes.

outcome.method_basis: Meister 1906 no. 40, the key printed for Morosini's nunciature (Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18), applied to DECODE's volunteer transcriptions. The character decode left garbled words in most lines; on 22 Oct 2026 a word-level decoder with a transcription-slip model and a hand re-parse of every break on the figures (and on the images where a figure was in doubt) turned 34 of the 35 enclosures into sentences, translated; most garbles were spurious nomenclator dots in the transcriptions and the clerk's -mente abbreviation (m + null 8). R35, a Spanish copy, still has too many holes.

title: The "nueva clave" of April 1911: four telegrams of the Maderista junta (San Antonio - El Paso) read in part with an 8 x 8 turning grille (preregistered measure failed; grille checked by a typed copy)
system.summary: An 8 x 8 turning grille (Fleissner) with 16 holes: blocks of 64 cipher letters written row by row and read through the holes, quarter turns clockwise, last block filled with nulls (x y z); the key was proposed by an AI model from the ciphertext and is not validated.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment on the sheets or in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1 (its p. 11 notes space for six telegrams still to be translated). No card of the fonds reads these telegrams.
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish. Claude (Opus) agents transcribed the telegrams from the CEHM viewer images and ran the preregistered measure; after the project's own attempts (columnar transposition, Caesar shifts, the cards of the fonds) failed, an AI model (Claude Fable 5.2, one API run, named in the contributor's files) proposed the grille and the readings from three telegrams, with one telegram held out; the agents checked the grille with an independent decoder and ran the measure once (failed). No human palaeographer checked the transcriptions. Issue #502 (SeldomPhooey, AI agents) added the held-out telegram's reading, the outside check and two transcription corrections; an independent session checked them against the images on 13 Nov 2026.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, Clave G.A. validation and readings, grille check and measure, write-up); Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), one API run on 1551.3-4, 1561.5-13 and 1569.3-10 (grille proposal and readings; pointed out the joined groups of 1561.7-13)
outcome.method_basis: The grille was proposed by an AI model in one API run from the ciphertext of three telegrams (the holes follow the nulls x/z of 1551.3-4) and checked here with an independent decoder; the held-out telegram was not sent. The preregistered measure on that telegram failed. An outside document, a typed period copy of 1569.3-10 (BNM), later agreed with the decryption on 174 of 176 letters and was not used to find the grille. The grille rests also on six 64-letter blocks that read as Spanish with no insertion or deletion, and on the first block of the held-out telegram.
outcome.validation.notes: The preregistered single measure on the held-out telegram CMXV.16.1561.3-13 FAILED: car4 = 0.520 against the 0.70 threshold, margin +0.118 over the best of 400 controls against the +0.30 required (200 random grilles at most 0.402, 200 shuffled texts at most 0.299); the lost letter in YPXB shifts block 2; the post-hoc trial is not counted. Contributor's own test, not docs/_validate.py; the cipher is now published (issue #502) but the measure was not re-run. Separately, an outside check succeeded: a typed period copy of 1569.3-10 (BNM, AMA Ms.M/T.2260 c.21) agrees with the grille's decryption on 174 of 176 letters; it was not used to find the grille.
outcome.verification: independent clear copy; statistical test; historical consistency
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration count by words (README rule), from reading.md, 13 Nov 2026: 77 words, 64 sure = 83% (1551.3-4 17 of 17, 1561.5-13 9 of 17, 1569.3-10 24 of 26, 1561.3-13 14 of 17; 10 probable, 3 unresolved are not counted as read). The first contributor's looser figure counts the probable words as read: 74 of 77 = 96%; SeldomPhooey's own figure for 1561.3-13 is 14 of 17 strict, 16 of 17 with the probable words.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.
conditions.tools: corpus.py (parser for the aligned decipherment); ctx.py (context viewer for unvalued groups); measure.py (coverage)

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.nomenclator.kinds: word parts; common words; names; titles
conditions.prior_solution.where: George Lasry's reconstructed key and segmented decipherment of the whole S364 corpus, both filed as attachments on every one of DECODE R154-R177; key dated 24 October 2020

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE session cookie used to download the record attachments.
outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.verification: key confirms; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Contents in print since 1897 (Kiewning). The key was not recovered by this project: every attack here failed. It is the key of the sibling volume Barb.lat. 6956, broken by Biermann and Bosbach in 2018 and on DECODE R215; George Lasry had identified that it also serves 6960. Applied 21 Sept 2026, it reads all 28 ciphertexts except ~1,750 three-digit nomenclator groups absent from the key. The earlier finding of deterministic variable-length groups stands and is explained by the key (2-digit + 3-digit + 1-digit nulls). The catalogue said 'what the cipher hides is not known'; it is known, and has been in print since 1897, from the Roman office's own decipherments. The cipher itself was not broken here and no partial key is claimed: a held-out test shows the table learned from R286 predicts unseen text no better than a shuffled control (0.355 vs 0.359), so the 55% consistency of the first pass was overfitting. A positive control on synthetic ciphertext recovers a random key 100/100 from a clean transcription, 87/100 at 0.5% digit error and 7/100 at 1.7%, so the method is sound and the limit is the transcription. Two explanations remain open and cannot be separated from this material: length errors in the transcription, or the cipher not being a fixed-width substitution of this plaintext. The run-length control then settled that: the longest consistent two-digit run is 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39 (synthetic at the same noise: 207), so there is no alignment signal and noise is not a sufficient explanation. R286 is not a two-digit homophonic encipherment of Kiewning's Nr. 153. Open: whether the code width differs, whether the sheet encodes another despatch or a materially different wording, or whether the system is nomenclator-heavy or variable-length. A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. What survives is either a variable-length nomenclator, or text that is not in print because Kiewning gives it only as German regest.

system.notes: 112,805 digits over the 28 ciphertexts. Digit frequencies are uneven (0 = 16.1%, 4 = 4.8%) and adjacent digits carry ~0.18 bits of mutual information, so the stream is structured. No phase preference was found for two-digit codes (IC 0.01462 at phase 0 vs 0.01466 at phase 1; even- and odd-position digit distributions agree to 0.2%) or for three-digit codes - though that phase test is inconclusive on its own, since ~1.7% digit slips randomise the phase; the calibrated corpus search is the sound version of the claim. distinct_symbols is the digit alphabet, not the key's code groups, which are unknown. A run-length control puts the longest consistent two-digit alignment to the known plaintext at 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39, where a synthetic two-digit cipher at the same transcription noise gives 207 - so the stream is not a two-digit substitution of that plaintext. CORRECTION 21 Sept 2026: the variable-length diagnosis was right, the rest of the system was not identified here. The key (sibling, 6956) mixes two-digit homophones, three-digit nomenclator groups and one-digit nulls 1/8, which is why every fixed-width test failed and why the repeat spectrum showed deterministic variable-length groups. distinct_symbols stays the digit alphabet; the key has ~127 known entries.

outcome.notes: Contents in print since 1897 (Kiewning). The key was not recovered by this project: every attack here failed. It is the key of the sibling volume Barb.lat. 6956, broken by Biermann and Bosbach in 2018 and on DECODE R215; George Lasry had identified that it also serves 6960. Applied 21 Sept 2026, it reads all 28 ciphertexts except ~1,750 three-digit nomenclator groups absent from the key. The earlier finding of deterministic variable-length groups stands and is explained by the key (2-digit + 3-digit + 1-digit nulls). The catalogue said 'what the cipher hides is not known'; it is known, and has been in print since 1897, from the Roman office's own decipherments. The cipher itself was not broken here and no partial key is claimed: a held-out test shows the table learned from R286 predicts unseen text no better than a shuffled control (0.355 vs 0.359), so the 55% consistency of the first pass was overfitting. A positive control on synthetic ciphertext recovers a random key 100/100 from a clean transcription, 87/100 at 0.5% digit error and 7/100 at 1.7%, so the method is sound and the limit is the transcription. Two explanations remain open and cannot be separated from this material: length errors in the transcription, or the cipher not being a fixed-width substitution of this plaintext. The run-length control then settled that: the longest consistent two-digit run is 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39 (synthetic at the same noise: 207), so there is no alignment signal and noise is not a sufficient explanation. R286 is not a two-digit homophonic encipherment of Kiewning's Nr. 153. Open: whether the code width differs, whether the sheet encodes another despatch or a materially different wording, or whether the system is nomenclator-heavy or variable-length. A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. What survives is either a variable-length nomenclator, or text that is not in print because Kiewning gives it only as German regest.
