outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...): pass by its own criteria. Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The project's verification of 12 Nov 2026 re-decoded the held-out lines (identical string) and scored them with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (best of 500 permuted keys) and -6.588 (best of 300 shuffles). The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

title: Christoffer Sehested's cipher letters from Vienna, January-May 1657 (catalogue 2520, Rigsarkivet TKUA Kejseren, unit 260651): German simple substitution in numbers with a nomenclator; 27 letters deciphered with the key of the contemporary gloss, 95.3% of tokens by the strict count
system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), pp. 238-245 and n. 62, who thanks Gigas for a private decipherment of Sehested's letters, never printed; one German phrase is quoted ("die Gemüther alhie nicht wenig ermunteret"). outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...): pass by its own criteria. Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The project's verification of 12 Nov 2026 re-decoded the held-out lines (identical string) and scored them with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (best of 500 permuted keys) and -6.588 (best of 300 shuffles). The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

title: Christoffer Sehested's cipher letters from Vienna, January-May 1657 (catalogue 2520, Rigsarkivet TKUA Kejseren, unit 260651): German simple substitution in numbers with a nomenclator; 27 letters deciphered with the key of the contemporary gloss, 95.3% of tokens by the strict count
system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), pp. 238-245 and n. 62, who thanks Gigas for a private decipherment of Sehested's letters, never printed; one German phrase is quoted ("die Gemüther alhie nicht wenig ermunteret"). outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...): pass by its own criteria. Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The project's verification of 12 Nov 2026 re-decoded the held-out lines (identical string) and scored them with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (best of 500 permuted keys) and -6.588 (best of 300 shuffles). The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

title: Christoffer Sehested's cipher letters from Vienna, January-May 1657 (catalogue 2520, Rigsarkivet TKUA Kejseren, unit 260651): German simple substitution in numbers with a nomenclator; 27 letters deciphered with the key of the contemporary gloss, 95.3% of tokens by the strict count
system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

title: Christoffer Sehested's cipher letters from Vienna, January-May 1657 (catalogue 2520, Rigsarkivet TKUA Kejseren, unit 260651): German simple substitution in numbers with a nomenclator; 27 letters deciphered with the key of the contemporary gloss, 95.3% of tokens by the strict count
system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), pp. 238-245 and n. 62, who thanks Gigas for a private decipherment of Sehested's letters, never printed; one German phrase is quoted ("die Gemüther alhie nicht wenig ermunteret"). outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...): pass by its own criteria. Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The project's verification of 12 Nov 2026 re-decoded the held-out lines (identical string) and scored them with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (best of 500 permuted keys) and -6.588 (best of 300 shuffles). The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

title: Christoffer Sehested's cipher letters from Vienna, January-May 1657 (catalogue 2520, Rigsarkivet TKUA Kejseren, unit 260651): German simple substitution in numbers with a nomenclator; 27 letters deciphered with the key of the contemporary gloss, 95.3% of tokens by the strict count
system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...): pass by its own criteria. Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The project's verification of 12 Nov 2026 re-decoded the held-out lines (identical string) and scored them with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (best of 500 permuted keys) and -6.588 (best of 300 shuffles). The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

title: Christoffer Sehested's cipher letters from Vienna, January-May 1657 (catalogue 2520, Rigsarkivet TKUA Kejseren, unit 260651): German simple substitution in numbers with a nomenclator; 27 letters deciphered with the key of the contemporary gloss, 95.3% of tokens by the strict count
system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.

Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), pp. 238-245 and n. 62, who thanks Gigas for a private decipherment of Sehested's letters, never printed; one German phrase is quoted ("die Gemüther alhie nicht wenig ermunteret"). outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".

system.sibling_key: Same cipher as Sessa's decrypted despatches of 1523-25 (ff. 138/140, 168-172, 322-324; R9897, R9893, R9834 and others); the key was rebuilt from them.

title: Sir Thomas Smith (France) to Cecil and the Queen, 1562/3-1566: 18 ciphered passages copied by Patrick Forbes, BL Add MS 4136 ff. 157-168 (DECODE R9248-R9254)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

title: Sir Thomas Smith (France) to Cecil and the Queen, 1562/3-1566: 18 ciphered passages copied by Patrick Forbes, BL Add MS 4136 ff. 157-168 (DECODE R9248-R9254)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

title: Sir Thomas Smith (France) to Cecil and the Queen, 1562/3-1566: 18 ciphered passages copied by Patrick Forbes, BL Add MS 4136 ff. 157-168 (DECODE R9248-R9254)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

title: Sir Thomas Smith (France) to Cecil and the Queen, 1562/3-1566: 18 ciphered passages copied by Patrick Forbes, BL Add MS 4136 ff. 157-168 (DECODE R9248-R9254)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic letter signs (37 sign types, including letter-pair signs) mixed with three-letter code groups for words, syllables and single letters (159 group types); word values such as que, por, papa, Italia, liga. Not the 1511-12 nomenclator.

I pp. 631-634 (lines 9-31 of the cipher). A clear draft, not a decipherment: no key was published.

outcome.method_basis: Michael Brackx recovered the sign alphabet ciphertext-only (joint annealing of sign and group values against a Spanish 5-gram, with an encipherment-cost term; no crib) and read 40 code-group types by context (issue #94, 23 Oct 2026); checked on a matched Lazarillo control and by docs/_validate.py (pass). He then found Terrateig 1963 vol. I pp. 631-634 quoting the letter from its minute, used the long quotation as a crib for ll. 9-31 (27 groups read, 11 tentative values confirmed, about 8 corrected) and four context rounds after it. The method stays key recovered from ciphertext-only (the alphabet and the first 40 groups came before the print was found); the code-group extension rests partly on external plaintext. The text is not read: 77 group tokens unread, look-alike readings 3.09% of letters.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Adrian of Utrecht (Cardinal of Tortosa) to Charles V, Valladolid, 9 September 1520: the cipher paragraph Danvila could not translate, read
system.summary: the Cardinal’s “dotted trigraph” code: consonant-vowel-consonant groups followed by a dot for words and syllables (gig. que, leb. no, sa. de, nof. los, mud. -mente…), and a homophonic alphabet of signs (h, ð, M = e; cf, 4, g, B× = a; ⊥, φ = r; y̥, p = s; ε̥ = t…). The same code in the letters of 1520 and 1521 (PTR,LEG,2,1,23, 30, 32, 61, 68, 73)
conditions.prior_solution.where: Danvila MHE XXXVI p. 18 ("no ha podido traducirse"); Bergenroth 1868; repository; Cryptiana (28 Oct 2026).
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from cipher/plain pairs of the Cardinal's other letters of 1520-21 (sign shapes re-read blind on plates); key K7 validated by a single measurement on a fresh held-out pair (2,1,99 vs Danvila).
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): key K7 frozen, then one measurement on a fresh pair named before download, AGS PTR,LEG,2,1,99 (2nd cipher passage, 10 lines frozen) against Danvila's printed plain text (MHE XXXVIII, 5 Dec 1521): 0.882 of characters (n = 170) against max 0.176 for 200 shuffled-key controls (median 0.041), rank 1/201; words 0.770 (controls max 0.119). Criterion fixed in advance: characters >= 0.85 and >= best control + 0.30. Earlier keys: K3 0.851 chars / 0.541 words on 2,1,68 (withdrawn), K4 0.783 on 2,1,85, K6 0.813 on 2,1,88 (failed).

title: Marie de Médicis (Brulart) to Savary de Brèves, Rome, 15 Sept and 10 Nov 1610 (BnF fr. 3789)
system.summary: Henri IV-Brèves cipher of 1610 (key BnF fr. 3462, Gallica view 112): homophonic alphabet of 2-5 signs per letter, comma-marked letter codes for common words, plain and overbarred number codes.

system.summary: System Y: a simple substitution with codes of one or two digits and no homophones. Even digits alone are vowels (0 i, 2 o, 4 e, 6 a); odd digits alone are m n s r (1 3 5 7); two-digit codes give the other consonants and u (13 z, 15 t, 17 l, 19 q, 29 p, 39 h, 49 g, 51 u, 59 f, 69 d, 79 c, 89 b); 8 and 9 alone, and 31, are nulls. system.summary: System Y: a simple substitution with codes of one or two digits and no homophones. Even digits alone are vowels (0 i, 2 o, 4 e, 6 a); odd digits alone are m n s r (1 3 5 7); two-digit codes give the other consonants and u (13 z, 15 t, 17 l, 19 q, 29 p, 39 h, 49 g, 51 u, 59 f, 69 d, 79 c, 89 b); 8 and 9 alone, and 31, are nulls. No word division; the text is parsed longest code first. The same system as Camillo Capilupi's letters c. 48 and c. 49r in capilupi1545. System X (03r, 09r) is a different hand and system, not attacked.

The contributor's count of certain + probable: 389/421 = 92.4% (384 on 11 Nov, 375/425 on 5 Nov); his recount by the looser rule of the 12 Nov integration (349/421 = 82.9%, which also counted 13 probable words read with the key): 363/421 = 86.2%. title: Plain standard telegraph code: 20 telegram(s) of Sun Yat-sen's circle intercepted in Japan, 29 December 1913 - 3 November 1916 (contributed by Brice Dudout)
system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Not in this repository (pointer only in sunyatsen/y1916); no decipherment on the JACAR copies; Cryptiana checked.
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules and re-read doubtful letters on the scans in blind panels; AI agents transcribed, searched the condenser family, decoded and translated.

system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. title: Plain standard telegraph code: 20 telegram(s) of Sun Yat-sen's circle intercepted in Japan, 29 December 1913 - 3 November 1916 (contributed by Brice Dudout)
system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).

system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).

system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).

system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. title: Plain standard telegraph code: 20 telegram(s) of Sun Yat-sen's circle intercepted in Japan, 29 December 1913 - 3 November 1916 (contributed by Brice Dudout)
system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).

system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. title: Dahku (signed 'Dahka') from Cracow, 1715 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/682): sign cipher in a Polish letter, key partial by our protocol, read in part
system.summary: Letter-for-letter substitution of Polish with graphic signs (Cyrillic- and Greek-like shapes, digits, a cross, a hash) and a few homophones (a = + / P, z = W / N, y = z / l, w = b / C); clear Polish words written among the cipher; a framed sign (N) and a tied sign (C) probably stand for names.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target, set the rules (protocol and pre-registration hashed before any key work, held-out lines, thresholds fixed in advance, one measurement) and answered a blind shape plate on one sign (shapes only, no values shown). outcome.method_basis: Key broken by annealing on the cipher of the training lines (clear words of the letter used only as word breaks) and measured once on held-out lines. Key 'partial' by our protocol (margin met, absolute threshold missed) and because two probable name signs have no value.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): transcription frozen, pre-registration hashed, key learned on lines d01-e02 and frozen, one measurement on e03-e06 (72 signs): M5 0.444 (share of decoded signs in Polish words of 5+ letters) vs 0.083 for the best of 200 shuffled keys, margin 0.361. system.summary: Substitution of Italian with homophones for the vowels (a: D, m; e: G, O, t, l; o: C, i and the groups oρ/oρo; i: u, n; u: 7 and ρ with a heavy dot), Latin, Greek-like and digit shapes for the consonants (4 = h, ʒ = d, d = f, ρ = l), word division kept; an isolated o is a null.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocol, partition and thresholds hashed before any calculation, one measurement). AI agents transcribed, broke the key, measured, read and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the reading.

outcome.method_basis: Key broken by annealing on the first eight cipher lines and validated once on the last three against an independent machine break of those lines; no clear text of the time exists.

title: Manuel Durón to W. Olliphant (González Garza), México to El Paso, 20 May 1911: warning against Licenciado Reyes Retana, read in part with a shift on a 29-sign alphabet (key not validated, text too short)
system.summary: A simple shift on a 29-sign Spanish alphabet (a b c ch d e f g h i j k l ll m n ñ o p q r s t u v w x y z): cipher = plain + 22; two header signs; the cipher sign ñ is typed 'n' by the telegraph, so cipher n reads t or u. Recovered from the ciphertext; not validated (107 signs).
conditions.prior_solution.where: No gloss on the sheet; absent from the typed list of period decipherments CMXV.18.1795.1 (45 pp., OCR searched: on 20 May only Elisa 1777.2-6, Herrera Moreno x2 and Miranda/Herrera Moreno; no 'Retana' outside Elisa). Catalogue 1462 lists 18.1777.1-6 as undeciphered; nothing in the issues (#330, #351) or PRs. Narváez 2019 (SRE book, ch. VII-VIII) could not be checked.
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish. title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

doc.plaintext.source: Clear copies exist: the cover letter on M37 roll 2 frames 395-396, the enclosed proposal on M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060. No contemporary decipherment on the frame. A few phrases are written in clear among the groups (lines 1-6).
doc.transcription.source: NARA M31 roll 14 frame 0039 (full frame and enlarged crops)
doc.transcription.notes: 26 written lines. 554 groups (552 numbers 1-1600, one group 5127 out of range, one group cut by the frame edge), counted by decode.py (groups joined by dots are counted one by one; python docs/_check_profile.py --measure counts words, not groups). Lines 1-6 and 10-12 read in a first pass, the rest in a second. A second agent re-read 144 groups blind (lines 3, 7, 9, 13, 18, 24 in full, parts of 12 and 17): 140 agree. Its three clear corrections (L9 721 for 724, L9 13 for 131, L24 608 for 108) are applied; L24 518 may be 548. About 74% of the groups were read once only.

system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in morris1813_transcription.txt (decode.py). Groups are joined by dots within a word and separated by a space between words. Marks under groups (5, 55, 5555, c, s) and a short double stroke after groups are transcribed; their meaning is not known. 361 and 364 (= JQA 1261, 1264) behave as comma and full stop, as in the Ellis 1839 alignment (open PR #107). From PR #200 on the readings use a surviving sheet of the code itself (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, NARA M97 roll 13, Weber's WE028) instead of the table rebuilt in ../jqa. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).

None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Over the thirteen texts worked: 2,609 coded words in the readings, 65 of them holes (word_share.py for the twelve letters in beling/letters/, 2,259 words and 55 holes, and the same rule by hand for frame 0039: 350 words, 10 holes). A hole is an unread group, a guessed [?word] or a word with supplied letters. Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 650, PR #114: the block reversal and frame 0039) and Andrew Beling, with AI agents (PR #200: the WE028 key sheet, five letters and frame 0039 reread; PR #415: Nos. 18, 19, 24, 25, 28). Integrated 12 Nov 2026: read_share on every letter is the word share of word_share.py (README read bar: unread groups, guessed words and supplied letters are holes); the contributor's own figure for the five PR #415 letters is a share of groups (0.981, 0.955, 0.980, 1.000, 1.000; beling/scripts/read_share.py). On frame 0039 it is the project's recount by the same rule (350 words, 10 holes, 0.971; Andrew Beling's count in PR #200 was 0.965, and the recount at integration, with 370 as a hole, 0.963). The Cevallos note and the No. 17 lines were transcribed and read at integration by one reader. codes_open covers the seven letters in the decode650 format (1,709 groups, 512 distinct): the groups with no reading at all are 575 and 1060. Rule of 12 Nov amended on 14 Nov 2026 (owner's decision, after Brice Dudout's observation in PR #570 and a look at the code sheet on NARA M97 roll 13 frames 1056-1057): the sign 370 is the eleventh and last entry of the sheet's list of punctuation marks and follows the full stop 364 at all 22 places, so it is punctuation, neither a word nor a hole; before that each [370] was one hole (2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967; No. 13 0.946, No. 19 0.943, No. 17 0.914; codes_open 3 open, 16 tokens). Nos. 13 and 19 are now over the 95% bar; No. 17 (0.941) is not, so the class stays read in part. The order of the contributor's work (numerals frozen before decoding) is by the contributor's record: the pull request is a single commit. Same code as ../jqa; Morris's block order is in block_map.tsv. 14 Nov 2026: the former target claiborne1806 (Brice Dudout, PR #564 and PR #581) is folded in under claiborne/ (one key, one entry): Claiborne's 1805 copy has the same reversed blocks. That part is in progress (the letters of 18 and 19 Nov 1806 at the Library of Congress and the printed edition were not seen); its texts are Wagner's decipherments and its figures (295 of 328 words mechanically) are kept apart from fraction_read, which covers the thirteen Morris texts only.

doc.plaintext.source: No contemporary decipherment noted on the copies. Woolfley (2013), Ebook Central p. 78, quotes the passage with small differences ('in short time', 'Not having the satisfaction', 'my discretion', 'in the present circumstances'); found after the reading (PR #200).

doc.transcription.notes: PR #200: two readers. The file also holds the letter of 27 January 1815; the count is of copy A (frame 0084). Groups counted at the integration of 12 Nov 2026 with a one-off regular expression over the named file (the copy named), not with docs/_check_profile.py --measure, because the file holds notes or more than one copy.
system.sibling_key: the JQA code, ../jqa/code_table.tsv (rebuilt there from the State Department clerk's decodes and Ford's printed decipherments of JQA's 1811-1812 despatches), applied unchanged under the block order in block_map.tsv
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in morris1813_transcription.txt (decode.py). Groups are joined by dots within a word and separated by a space between words. Marks under groups (5, 55, 5555, c, s) and a short double stroke after groups are transcribed; their meaning is not known. 361 and 364 (= JQA 1261, 1264) behave as comma and full stop, as in the Ellis 1839 alignment (open PR #107). From PR #200 on the readings use a surviving sheet of the code itself (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, NARA M97 roll 13, Weber's WE028) instead of the table rebuilt in ../jqa. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 650) and the rules for the first contribution; Andrew Beling directed the AI agents of PR #200 and PR #415 and recorded the reading review of frame 0039. The agents fetched the frames, transcribed, matched the tables, decoded and read. No person has checked a passage against the image without AI as far as the records show.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription; AI agents directed by Andrew Beling (PR #200, PR #415); an AI agent at the integration of 12 Nov 2026; Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout (Claiborne letters, PR #564 and PR #581)
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The JQA code table (../jqa/code_table.tsv), rebuilt in targets/jqa for JQA's 1811-1812 St Petersburg despatches and not tied to Morris, found here to fit Morris's groups once his sixteen blocks of 100 are taken in reverse order (block_map.tsv, recovered from the ciphertext).
outcome.verification: independent verification; matched control; historical consistency; contemporary decipherment
outcome.fraction_read_source: Over the thirteen texts worked: 2,609 coded words in the readings, 65 of them holes (word_share.py for the twelve letters in beling/letters/, 2,259 words and 55 holes, and the same rule by hand for frame 0039: 350 words, 10 holes). A hole is an unread group, a guessed [?word] or a word with supplied letters. Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 650, PR #114: the block reversal and frame 0039) and Andrew Beling, with AI agents (PR #200: the WE028 key sheet, five letters and frame 0039 reread; PR #415: Nos. 18, 19, 24, 25, 28). Integrated 12 Nov 2026: read_share on every letter is the word share of word_share.py (README read bar: unread groups, guessed words and supplied letters are holes); the contributor's own figure for the five PR #415 letters is a share of groups (0.981, 0.955, 0.980, 1.000, 1.000; beling/scripts/read_share.py). On frame 0039 it is the project's recount by the same rule (350 words, 10 holes, 0.971; Andrew Beling's count in PR #200 was 0.965, and the recount at integration, with 370 as a hole, 0.963). The Cevallos note and the No. 17 lines were transcribed and read at integration by one reader. codes_open covers the seven letters in the decode650 format (1,709 groups, 512 distinct): the groups with no reading at all are 575 and 1060. Rule of 12 Nov amended on 14 Nov 2026 (owner's decision, after Brice Dudout's observation in PR #570 and a look at the code sheet on NARA M97 roll 13 frames 1056-1057): the sign 370 is the eleventh and last entry of the sheet's list of punctuation marks and follows the full stop 364 at all 22 places, so it is punctuation, neither a word nor a hole; before that each [370] was one hole (2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967; No. 13 0.946, No. 19 0.943, No. 17 0.914; codes_open 3 open, 16 tokens). Nos. 13 and 19 are now over the 95% bar; No. 17 (0.941) is not, so the class stays read in part. The order of the contributor's work (numerals frozen before decoding) is by the contributor's record: the pull request is a single commit. Same code as ../jqa; Morris's block order is in block_map.tsv. 14 Nov 2026: the former target claiborne1806 (Brice Dudout, PR #564 and PR #581) is folded in under claiborne/ (one key, one entry): Claiborne's 1805 copy has the same reversed blocks. That part is in progress (the letters of 18 and 19 Nov 1806 at the Library of Congress and the printed edition were not seen); its texts are Wagner's decipherments and its figures (295 of 328 words mechanically) are kept apart from fraction_read, which covers the thirteen Morris texts only.

Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), Ebook Central pp. 98-99, quotes three coded passages (the arrests; the king and 'those two classes'; the understanding between the Spanish and English cabinets) and paraphrases the Inquisition passage; found after the reading. Differences from the decode: 'those' for 'these', 'sufficient' for 'sufficiently good', 'on this ...' for 'on these or any other subjects'.
doc.transcription.source: NARA M31 roll 14 frames 0112-0113; Triplicate 0117-0118 collated in full, 0129 at the disputed places (collation_other_copies.txt)
doc.transcription.notes: Transcribed 11 Nov 2026 from full-resolution crops before decoding, with no key open; the hashes were frozen before decoding (beling/SHA256SUMS.txt). One reader. Groups counted by beling/scripts/read_share.py (heading, body and signature; groups joined by dots counted one by one).
system.sibling_key: the JQA code, ../jqa/code_table.tsv (rebuilt there from the State Department clerk's decodes and Ford's printed decipherments of JQA's 1811-1812 despatches), applied unchanged under the block order in block_map.tsv
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in morris1813_transcription.txt (decode.py). Groups are joined by dots within a word and separated by a space between words. Marks under groups (5, 55, 5555, c, s) and a short double stroke after groups are transcribed; their meaning is not known. 361 and 364 (= JQA 1261, 1264) behave as comma and full stop, as in the Ellis 1839 alignment (open PR #107). From PR #200 on the readings use a surviving sheet of the code itself (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, NARA M97 roll 13, Weber's WE028) instead of the table rebuilt in ../jqa. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 650) and the rules for the first contribution; Andrew Beling directed the AI agents of PR #200 and PR #415 and recorded the reading review of frame 0039. The agents fetched the frames, transcribed, matched the tables, decoded and read. No person has checked a passage against the image without AI as far as the records show.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription; AI agents directed by Andrew Beling (PR #200, PR #415); an AI agent at the integration of 12 Nov 2026; Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout (Claiborne letters, PR #564 and PR #581)
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The JQA code table (../jqa/code_table.tsv), rebuilt in targets/jqa for JQA's 1811-1812 St Petersburg despatches and not tied to Morris, found here to fit Morris's groups once his sixteen blocks of 100 are taken in reverse order (block_map.tsv, recovered from the ciphertext).
outcome.verification: independent verification; matched control; historical consistency; contemporary decipherment
outcome.fraction_read_source: Over the thirteen texts worked: 2,609 coded words in the readings, 65 of them holes (word_share.py for the twelve letters in beling/letters/, 2,259 words and 55 holes, and the same rule by hand for frame 0039: 350 words, 10 holes). A hole is an unread group, a guessed [?word] or a word with supplied letters. Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

doc.plaintext.source: A State Department clerk wrote the Spanish between the lines of the copy on frames 0169-0170. It was seen at reduced size before the numerals on 0115-0116 were transcribed, and looked at closely at four places afterwards (elev son, ep for, particulares, 17). The clerk's text is not transcribed here. By a web search result of 12 Nov 2026, an annotation in the Papers of James Madison (Founders Online, Madison/03-08-02-0355) says Erving's letter to Monroe of 4 December 1814 enclosed a copy and translation of this note; the page could not be opened here.

doc.transcription.notes: Transcribed 12 Nov 2026 at the integration of PR #415. Not blind: the clerk's words on 0169-0170 had been seen at reduced size. One reader. Marks under the groups read approximately. One group corrected after decoding with the copy on 0169 in view (116.05: 1301, first read 1307). Groups counted with beling/scripts/decode650.py (heading, body and signature).

system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in morris1813_transcription.txt (decode.py). Groups are joined by dots within a word and separated by a space between words. Marks under groups (5, 55, 5555, c, s) and a short double stroke after groups are transcribed; their meaning is not known. 361 and 364 (= JQA 1261, 1264) behave as comma and full stop, as in the Ellis 1839 alignment (open PR #107). From PR #200 on the readings use a surviving sheet of the code itself (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, NARA M97 roll 13, Weber's WE028) instead of the table rebuilt in ../jqa. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
