outcome.method_basis: The JQA code table (../jqa/code_table.tsv), rebuilt in targets/jqa for JQA's 1811-1812 St Petersburg despatches and not tied to Morris, found here to fit Morris's groups once his sixteen blocks of 100 are taken in reverse order (block_map.tsv, recovered from the ciphertext).
outcome.verification: independent verification; matched control; historical consistency; contemporary decipherment
outcome.fraction_read_source: Over the thirteen texts worked: 2,609 coded words in the readings, 65 of them holes (word_share.py for the twelve letters in beling/letters/, 2,259 words and 55 holes, and the same rule by hand for frame 0039: 350 words, 10 holes). A hole is an unread group, a guessed [?word] or a word with supplied letters. Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

The Cevallos note and the No. 17 lines were transcribed and read at integration by one reader. codes_open covers the seven letters in the decode650 format (1,709 groups, 512 distinct): the groups with no reading at all are 575 and 1060. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Over the thirteen texts worked: 2,609 coded words in the readings, 65 of them holes (word_share.py for the twelve letters in beling/letters/, 2,259 words and 55 holes, and the same rule by hand for frame 0039: 350 words, 10 holes). Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).

system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in morris1813_transcription.txt (decode.py). Groups are joined by dots within a word and separated by a space between words. Marks under groups (5, 55, 5555, c, s) and a short double stroke after groups are transcribed; their meaning is not known. 361 and 364 (= JQA 1261, 1264) behave as comma and full stop, as in the Ellis 1839 alignment (open PR #107). From PR #200 on the readings use a surviving sheet of the code itself (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, NARA M97 roll 13, Weber's WE028) instead of the table rebuilt in ../jqa. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 650) and the rules for the first contribution; Andrew Beling directed the AI agents of PR #200 and PR #415 and recorded the reading review of frame 0039. The agents fetched the frames, transcribed, matched the tables, decoded and read. No person has checked a passage against the image without AI as far as the records show.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription; AI agents directed by Andrew Beling (PR #200, PR #415); an AI agent at the integration of 12 Nov 2026; Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout (Claiborne letters, PR #564 and PR #581)
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The JQA code table (../jqa/code_table.tsv), rebuilt in targets/jqa for JQA's 1811-1812 St Petersburg despatches and not tied to Morris, found here to fit Morris's groups once his sixteen blocks of 100 are taken in reverse order (block_map.tsv, recovered from the ciphertext).
outcome.verification: independent verification; matched control; historical consistency; contemporary decipherment
outcome.fraction_read_source: Over the thirteen texts worked: 2,609 coded words in the readings, 65 of them holes (word_share.py for the twelve letters in beling/letters/, 2,259 words and 55 holes, and the same rule by hand for frame 0039: 350 words, 10 holes). A hole is an unread group, a guessed [?word] or a word with supplied letters. Since 14 Nov 2026 the sign 370 is counted as punctuation, neither word nor hole (22 places; before that 2,631 words, 87 holes, 0.967). This is a share of words, not of groups, and it does not cover the other coded frames of the roll, which are further copies or carry a clerk's decipherment and were not worked here.

The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)
system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

title: Moscow 1940: Soviet enciphered weather broadcasts read by the Japanese Army (1938-1940), key tables transcribed and checked
system.summary: Additive/subtractive superencipherment, figure by figure without carrying, of the international synoptic weather code; four generations 1938-1940: fixed additive with group exchange (1938), per-group additives (1938-39), autokey on a substituted first group (Far East 1940), indicator-dependent subtractor (Moscow types 17040...05188, Feb-June 1940), and from June 1940 a 109-figure cycle with an indicator group aaabb in clear (two tables, odd and even days)
conditions.prior_solution.where: the Japanese Army Meteorological Department's reports themselves (methods, keys, tables, worked examples)
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout found the file among the JACAR searches on Japanese intercepts, set the rules (transcribe and freeze the tables before any check, test on the reports' own held-out examples), and settled doubtful figures by targeted visual review (shapes only); AI agents transcribed, checked and wrote up.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method_basis: Keys, tables and methods recovered by the Japanese Army Meteorological Department in 1938-1940 and given in its reports; transcribed and checked here.
outcome.validation.notes: No key recovered by us and no language read: the keys are Japanese; checked on the reports' own held-out examples (60/60, 25/25) and on Audric's example (25/25).
outcome.fraction_read_source: June-July tables: 4,793 of 4,796 figures certain, 3 restored, 0 unresolved; worked example 60/60 figures.

title: King Joseph to Napoleon, December 1812 (catalogued as Berthier to Napoleon, 22 Dec 1812)
system.summary: Numeric code of about 1200 groups (2-1388): the Grand Chiffre of 1812, whose deciphering table is at the SHD (B n. 30). Several numbers per frequent word (de = 13, 544, 710, 989, 1060); syllables and letters for the rest.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Ilia Chirtulov found that the Great Cipher of 1812 reads it and that the writer is King Joseph (received by S. Tomokiyo 4 Oct 2026, reported on Cryptiana 12 Oct 2026); Brice Dudout's re-reading was independent of it.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded. Second phase (Brice Dudout, 12 Oct 2026): chose the key, froze the table entries, re-read the plate and set the control; Claude (Anthropic) agents helped with the decoding and write-up; model versions not recorded.

title: The Count-Duke of Olivares to the Duke of Alba, Madrid, 22 August 1626 (lead 1273): Philip IV's general cipher A, read; key partial by our protocol
system.summary: Philip IV's general cipher 'A' (as used with the 2nd Marquis of Santa Cruz, 1629-1632): homophonic syllabary of letter groups (fer, xer, pon, tor ...), numbers for letters and syllables, special signs, and a nomenclator of numbers and groups for words (fro = Dios, 199 = hija, ber = servicio ...).
conditions.prior_solution.where: DECODE R1190 lists this letter (BNE MSS/10249, Madrid 22 Aug 1626) with status 'Decrypted' and an inline-plaintext flag; checked at DECODE level 2 on 5 Nov 2026: the record has 3 images of BNE MSS/10249 (added 13 Jul 2021), an empty documents list, no transcription, no key and no decipherer; no plaintext is written on the pages. Where the 'Decrypted' status comes from is unknown (your vetting note of 4 Nov 2026 on lead 1273 relies on that status). No edition found: Elliott & de la Peña, Memoriales y cartas del Conde Duque de Olivares (2013 ed.), table of contents: the only 1626 piece is doc. XI to the King; no letter to Alba. Nothing at Tomokiyo's or on the web.
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the lead and set the rules (protocol hashed before any measurement, one measurement on a held-out part, no change to the measured key or transcription); he answered a blind pre-registered proof-reading of 13 sign forms (none from the held-out part) and decided, after the measurement, to read the three 'hol' of the held-out part by the value so established, counted as probable. AI agents transcribed, measured, read and wrote up.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The general cipher A rebuilt from Santa Cruz pairs of 1630-32 (targets/santacruz1630, K6A) reads the training part of this letter; 20 values were added from that part only, then the key was frozen and measured once on the held-out part.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; sender or date identified
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py), one measurement: M5 (share of decoded letters covered by Spanish words of >= 5 letters) 0.506 on H (542 tokens) against 0.144 for the best of 200 keys shuffled within length classes (amendment written before H was transcribed). Criterion fixed in advance: >= 0.60 and >= best control + 0.30. Margin met (0.362), threshold not: partial by our protocol. M5 of a perfect contemporary plaintext of the same series is 0.636, so 0.60 asks for about 95% correctness.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words not counted as read), counted by script on the marked reading (reading.md): 1,001 cipher words: 906 certain, 47 probable, 13 restored, 35 unresolved = 953/1,001 = 95.2%. About 54 line ends lost in the gutter (ff. 13v, 14v) are not counted. The three 'hol' of the held-out part are among the probable words (value established outside it).

title: Francesco Pandolfini's letters from the French court, Dec 1514 - Mar 1515, in cipher (ASF MAP LXXII 307, 309, 310, 311, 322, 333): one passage read, five read in part; key partial (catalogue 2389)
system.summary: Consonant signs with the vowel written as a superscript figure (1-5 = u, o, i, e, a), bare vowel signs, homophones, word signs (F = et, M = non, T = senza) and a numeric nomenclator between points (.2. papa, .4. Cristianissimo, .64. Santita), between clear passages.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of the time for 307, 309, 310, 311 or 322 (Daniel Bourdeau's vetting of 6 Nov 2026; neighbours and the untitled clear copies checked on 9 Nov 2026; 316 is the clear of 315, not of 310); for 333 the same news is given in clear in 332 (copy to the Otto of the same day). Not in Desjardins-Canestrini, Negociations diplomatiques de la France avec la Toscane, vol. II (1861), which has a gap from 16 Aug 1514 to 25 May 1515. Catalogue 2389 open, no target or PR by anyone else in this repository (re-checked 9 Nov 2026).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau found the six bare letters and the pairs of the same system (lead 2389). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocols hashed before each held-out transcription, one measurement each, thresholds fixed in advance; transcriptions hashed before decoding). AI agents transcribed, built and merged the keys, measured and read. No human palaeographer checked the transcriptions.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key was learnt from cipher/decipherment pairs of the time in the same filza, measured on held-out pairs (partial at best), extended by declared derived values (v4, v6), then applied to the bare letters 307, 309, 310, 311, 322 and 333, which have no decipherment.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py): P01 0.788 and P02 0.691 under 0.85 (not validated); P03bis n-gram N 0.613, partial under a lenient threshold. Keys v4 and v6 derived after measurement, not measured.

title: Francesco Pandolfini's letters from the French court, Dec 1514 - Mar 1515, in cipher (ASF MAP LXXII 307, 309, 310, 311, 322, 333): one passage read, five read in part; key partial (catalogue 2389)
system.summary: Consonant signs with the vowel written as a superscript figure (1-5 = u, o, i, e, a), bare vowel signs, homophones, word signs (F = et, M = non, T = senza) and a numeric nomenclator between points (.2. papa, .4. Cristianissimo, .64. Santita), between clear passages.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment of the time for 307, 309, 310, 311 or 322 (Daniel Bourdeau's vetting of 6 Nov 2026; neighbours and the untitled clear copies checked on 9 Nov 2026; 316 is the clear of 315, not of 310); for 333 the same news is given in clear in 332 (copy to the Otto of the same day). Not in Desjardins-Canestrini, Negociations diplomatiques de la France avec la Toscane, vol. II (1861), which has a gap from 16 Aug 1514 to 25 May 1515. Catalogue 2389 open, no target or PR by anyone else in this repository (re-checked 9 Nov 2026).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau found the six bare letters and the pairs of the same system (lead 2389). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocols hashed before each held-out transcription, one measurement each, thresholds fixed in advance; transcriptions hashed before decoding). AI agents transcribed, built and merged the keys, measured and read. No human palaeographer checked the transcriptions.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key was learnt from cipher/decipherment pairs of the time in the same filza, measured on held-out pairs (partial at best), extended by declared derived values (v4, v6), then applied to the bare letters 307, 309, 310, 311, 322 and 333, which have no decipherment.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py): P01 0.788 and P02 0.691 under 0.85 (not validated); P03bis n-gram N 0.613, partial under a lenient threshold. Keys v4 and v6 derived after measurement, not measured.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Words read by sense (certain + probable) over all six bare letters, about 1,740 of about 2,170: 322 about 129/168, 307 262/291, 309 75/83, 310 about 800/1,065 (unresolved groups counted as 3 words), 311 about 440/534, 333 29/29; word boundaries are not written, so the counts are approximate.

title: Richard Taylor telegram books: January–March alignments, recipient-specific key use and unresolved transcription (catalogue 681; in progress)
system.summary: Confederate Vigenere with selected words enciphered using COME RETRIBUTION, COMPLETE VICTORY, or THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; the key advances over cipher letters only.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2. Further prior plaintext: OR I/45/2 p.772 (9 January), I/49/2 pp.1223 and1255 (10 and20 April), and an undated pencil interlinear decipherment over the 9 March Wirt Adams order.
conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded. Bryan Payne (bdpayne) selected catalogue 681, directed the continuation and authorized submission; transcription, analysis and writing by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), no subagents or independent human reading review claimed.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); OpenAI Codex (GPT-6); Claude (Anthropic) agents run by Brice Dudout (blind transcription, pre-registration, measure and readings of vol. 196 fr. 0030 and 0031-0032)
outcome.method_basis: The key COMERETRIBUTION was already identified for this correspondence: catalogue entry 681 had read frame 0061 and the vol. 11 OCR runs with it, and it is the known key of Confederate telegraph traffic in 1864-65. It was applied to each telegram from its first cipher letter, word by word; two of the four telegrams are printed in clear in OR I/49/2. Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; key recovered; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: key confirms; independent clear copy; historical consistency

Includes existing printed and pencil decipherments, known-key contextual readings and earlier key recovery from external plaintext. New November 9 work covers seven further messages; see REPORT-2026-11-09.md and WORKLOG.md. March 8–9 recipient-specific evidence does not establish a universal key switch. Overall fraction unknown: remaining passages across three volumes are not exhaustively inventoried. No complete-target or novel-plaintext claim; model reviews are not independent handwriting verification. 15 Nov 2026 (PR #676): two further telegrams entered; the 11 April lower telegram uses a fifth key, RALLY TO THE FRONT, recovered from the ciphertext alone (method for that document: key recovered from ciphertext-only), not found in any key list opened.

system.summary: Confederate Vigenere with selected words enciphered using COME RETRIBUTION, COMPLETE VICTORY, or THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; the key advances over cipher letters only.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2. Further prior plaintext: OR I/45/2 p.772 (9 January), I/49/2 pp.1223 and1255 (10 and20 April), and an undated pencil interlinear decipherment over the 9 March Wirt Adams order.
conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded. Bryan Payne (bdpayne) selected catalogue 681, directed the continuation and authorized submission; transcription, analysis and writing by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), no subagents or independent human reading review claimed.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); OpenAI Codex (GPT-6); Claude (Anthropic) agents run by Brice Dudout (blind transcription, pre-registration, measure and readings of vol. 196 fr. 0030 and 0031-0032)
outcome.method_basis: The key COMERETRIBUTION was already identified for this correspondence: catalogue entry 681 had read frame 0061 and the vol. 11 OCR runs with it, and it is the known key of Confederate telegraph traffic in 1864-65. It was applied to each telegram from its first cipher letter, word by word; two of the four telegrams are printed in clear in OR I/49/2. Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; key recovered; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: key confirms; independent clear copy; historical consistency

Includes existing printed and pencil decipherments, known-key contextual readings and earlier key recovery from external plaintext. New November 9 work covers seven further messages; see REPORT-2026-11-09.md and WORKLOG.md. March 8–9 recipient-specific evidence does not establish a universal key switch. Overall fraction unknown: remaining passages across three volumes are not exhaustively inventoried. system.summary: Confederate Vigenere with selected words enciphered using COME RETRIBUTION, COMPLETE VICTORY, or THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; the key advances over cipher letters only.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2. Further prior plaintext: OR I/45/2 p.772 (9 January), I/49/2 pp.1223 and1255 (10 and20 April), and an undated pencil interlinear decipherment over the 9 March Wirt Adams order.
conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded. Bryan Payne (bdpayne) selected catalogue 681, directed the continuation and authorized submission; transcription, analysis and writing by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), no subagents or independent human reading review claimed.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); OpenAI Codex (GPT-6); Claude (Anthropic) agents run by Brice Dudout (blind transcription, pre-registration, measure and readings of vol. 196 fr. 0030 and 0031-0032)
outcome.method_basis: The key COMERETRIBUTION was already identified for this correspondence: catalogue entry 681 had read frame 0061 and the vol. 11 OCR runs with it, and it is the known key of Confederate telegraph traffic in 1864-65. It was applied to each telegram from its first cipher letter, word by word; two of the four telegrams are printed in clear in OR I/49/2. Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; key recovered; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: key confirms; independent clear copy; historical consistency

Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.

Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.

The clerks' capitals mislead in a few recurring ways (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, a U-like glyph for IC); every correction is a single glyph and is listed in alignment.tsv.
conditions.tools: decrypt.py (Vigenere decryption over alignment.tsv, controls); continue_analysis.py (candidate/reconstruction alignment and key controls); NARA images and catalog OCR; Internet Archive Official Records OCR

title: Richard Taylor telegram books: January–March alignments, recipient-specific key use and unresolved transcription (catalogue 681; in progress)
system.summary: Confederate Vigenere with selected words enciphered using COME RETRIBUTION, COMPLETE VICTORY, or THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; the key advances over cipher letters only.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2. Further prior plaintext: OR I/45/2 p.772 (9 January), I/49/2 pp.1223 and1255 (10 and20 April), and an undated pencil interlinear decipherment over the 9 March Wirt Adams order.
conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded. Bryan Payne (bdpayne) selected catalogue 681, directed the continuation and authorized submission; transcription, analysis and writing by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), no subagents or independent human reading review claimed.
conditions.models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); OpenAI Codex (GPT-6); Claude (Anthropic) agents run by Brice Dudout (blind transcription, pre-registration, measure and readings of vol. 196 fr. 0030 and 0031-0032)
outcome.method_basis: The key COMERETRIBUTION was already identified for this correspondence: catalogue entry 681 had read frame 0061 and the vol. 11 OCR runs with it, and it is the known key of Confederate telegraph traffic in 1864-65. It was applied to each telegram from its first cipher letter, word by word; two of the four telegrams are printed in clear in OR I/49/2. Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; key recovered; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: key confirms; independent clear copy; historical consistency

title: Wackerbarth's cipher letters, 1715-1717 (HStA Dresden 10026 Loc. 00712/05 and 00713/01): one key rebuilt from the glosses of the time; Relation XXII from Vienna to Augustus II (14-16 June 1717) and the letter of 20 November 1715 from the camp before Stralsund read in part; the letter to Flemming of 24 April 1717 read from its decipherment of the time (contributed by Brice Dudout; simultaneous work: A.-S. Rous)
system.summary: Saxon system S1 of Wackerbarth's letters of 1715 and of his Vienna mission (March-June 1717), one key: homophonic substitution of French letters in 1-2 digit numbers (e 2/10, i 9, o 16/22/33, t 28/52 ...), polygrams and a nomenclator in 3-digit numbers (154 Votre Excellence, 177 le Czar, 187 le roi de Suède, 217 le roi d'Angleterre, 252 le roi de Prusse, 292 la Pologne, 306 Vienne, 355 premier), 4-digit numbers taken for nulls, clear words interspersed.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Many S1 passages of both volumes carry interlinear decipherments of the time (the keys were rebuilt from them); the letter of 24 April 1717 has a decipherment sheet of the time (ff. 33-33v). Relation XXII and the letter of 20 Nov. 1715 have none (a few marginal words on the latter). A.-S. Rous (The Keys of Diplomacy, HistoCrypt 2024, University of Tartu repository) works on this correspondence; by the contributor's report of her paper she lists the 1717 letter as not deciphered. The paper could not be opened at integration (12 Nov 2026; abstract only), so this is not checked. An original key may survive: DECODE holds the Saxon key series of Loc. 03233/02 (not tried on S1), and a search snippet of Rous's 2022 book mentions Wackerbarth-Flemming nomenclators for the 1717 Vienna trip (book not opened).
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocols hashed before each single measurement; a partial reading may be published if explained); on 11 Nov 2026, after the second measurement, he decided to accept the held-out language test alone as the condition for reading Relation XXII (post hoc, declared). Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, built the key, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading against the scans. For the letter of 20 Nov. 1715 he answered once a blind plate of digit shapes (W1, two controls passed) and approved adding the letter to this target.

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the interlinear glosses of the time on other letters in the same key: key c from views 0017, 0057-0062, 0071-0072, 0080-0081 and 0086-0088 of Loc. 00713/01, K1715 from views 0388-0390 of Loc. 00712/05. It was then applied to Relation XXII and to the letter of 20 Nov. 1715, which have no decipherment. The sheet of 24 April 1717 was not a source of the key.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests, not docs/_validate.py. The declared ground-truth test A' FAILED: 0.339 of gloss words exact on the held-out letter of 28 May 1717 against 0.128 for the best of 200 permuted keys, margin 0.21 where 0.30 and a score of 0.60 were required. The protocol required A' and the language test B' both; B' passed (view 0091, z = 11.5). Reading on B' alone is a rule changed after the result (Avenant 3). A first protocol (tests A and B) had also failed. Hence 'weak', not 'pass'. Other evidence, separate from the failed test: the 1715 letter's own pre-registered measurement passed (S 0.945 against 0.730, rank 1 of 401); and, checked at verification on 12 Nov 2026, each volume's key reads the other volume's letter (K1715 on Relation XXII: z = 8.8 over 2,939 groups; key c on the 1715 letter: z = 5.6), and every permuted-key control is beaten on every document with either key. Order of events by the contributor's record (all commits and timestamps are of 11 Nov 2026).

doc.transcription.notes: Transcribed by Claude Opus 5.5 agents (main agent views 0089-0090, three sub-agents 0091-0099), 11 Nov 2026, each part hashed before any decoding of it and never corrected from the sense. Three numbers are probably misread (0097 G07 174 for 177, 0097 G15 4 for 7, 0098 G03 184 for 187): noted in reading.md, left as frozen. No blind re-reading yet. Verification (12 Nov 2026): view 0091 left page, lines G02-G20 (about 190 groups), compared with the archive image, all agree; views 0096 and 0042 not compared; the three suspected 4/7 misreadings not re-read.
system.notes: One key in both volumes: key c (glosses of Loc. 00713/01) and K1715 (glosses of Loc. 00712/05) agree on 43 of their 47 common numbers by the verifier's comparison (the contributor counted 47 of 50), share 150, 168 and 700, and each reads the other volume's letter (verification, 12 Nov 2026). The four that differ: 20 (ee / b; b is right), 71 (y / i; the training glosses have y in all 8 cases, so s15_key.tsv's 'i' is a slip), 77 (ss / s), 97 (m / la). Key c's 103 = 'les' reads 'le' in Relation XXII ('le comte de Sinzendorf'). S1 is not the Flemming key K0 (Loc. 00675/10, view 0080), nor its shifted variant, nor Wackerbarth's 1703 key (contributor's comparison). The volume's Nov.-Dec. 1717 letters use another key (S2 = K0); they are outside this entry. By the contributor's report of A.-S. Rous's paper (not opened here), she describes the 1717 system as substitution in 1-3 digit numbers, mostly 2, with 355 and 1000 in the nomenclator.

title: Wackerbarth's cipher letters, 1715-1717 (HStA Dresden 10026 Loc. 00712/05 and 00713/01): one key rebuilt from the glosses of the time; Relation XXII from Vienna to Augustus II (14-16 June 1717) and the letter of 20 November 1715 from the camp before Stralsund read in part; the letter to Flemming of 24 April 1717 read from its decipherment of the time (contributed by Brice Dudout; simultaneous work: A.-S. Rous)
system.summary: Saxon system S1 of Wackerbarth's letters of 1715 and of his Vienna mission (March-June 1717), one key: homophonic substitution of French letters in 1-2 digit numbers (e 2/10, i 9, o 16/22/33, t 28/52 ...), polygrams and a nomenclator in 3-digit numbers (154 Votre Excellence, 177 le Czar, 187 le roi de Suède, 217 le roi d'Angleterre, 252 le roi de Prusse, 292 la Pologne, 306 Vienne, 355 premier), 4-digit numbers taken for nulls, clear words interspersed.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Many S1 passages of both volumes carry interlinear decipherments of the time (the keys were rebuilt from them); the letter of 24 April 1717 has a decipherment sheet of the time (ff. 33-33v). Relation XXII and the letter of 20 Nov. 1715 have none (a few marginal words on the latter). A.-S. Rous (The Keys of Diplomacy, HistoCrypt 2024, University of Tartu repository) works on this correspondence; by the contributor's report of her paper she lists the 1717 letter as not deciphered. The paper could not be opened at integration (12 Nov 2026; abstract only), so this is not checked. An original key may survive: DECODE holds the Saxon key series of Loc. 03233/02 (not tried on S1), and a search snippet of Rous's 2022 book mentions Wackerbarth-Flemming nomenclators for the 1717 Vienna trip (book not opened).
conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocols hashed before each single measurement; a partial reading may be published if explained); on 11 Nov 2026, after the second measurement, he decided to accept the held-out language test alone as the condition for reading Relation XXII (post hoc, declared). Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, built the key, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading against the scans. For the letter of 20 Nov. 1715 he answered once a blind plate of digit shapes (W1, two controls passed) and approved adding the letter to this target.
conditions.models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, key, protocols, measurements, reading, write-up)
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the interlinear glosses of the time on other letters in the same key: key c from views 0017, 0057-0062, 0071-0072, 0080-0081 and 0086-0088 of Loc. 00713/01, K1715 from views 0388-0390 of Loc. 00712/05. It was then applied to Relation XXII and to the letter of 20 Nov. 1715, which have no decipherment. The sheet of 24 April 1717 was not a source of the key.
outcome.validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests, not docs/_validate.py. The declared ground-truth test A' FAILED: 0.339 of gloss words exact on the held-out letter of 28 May 1717 against 0.128 for the best of 200 permuted keys, margin 0.21 where 0.30 and a score of 0.60 were required. The protocol required A' and the language test B' both; B' passed (view 0091, z = 11.5). Reading on B' alone is a rule changed after the result (Avenant 3). A first protocol (tests A and B) had also failed. Hence 'weak', not 'pass'. Other evidence, separate from the failed test: the 1715 letter's own pre-registered measurement passed (S 0.945 against 0.730, rank 1 of 401); and, checked at verification on 12 Nov 2026, each volume's key reads the other volume's letter (K1715 on Relation XXII: z = 8.8 over 2,939 groups; key c on the 1715 letter: z = 5.6), and every permuted-key control is beaten on every document with either key. Order of events by the contributor's record (all commits and timestamps are of 11 Nov 2026).
outcome.verification: statistical test; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency
outcome.fraction_read_source: integration_recount.py over reading files and frozen transcriptions, cipher words of the two letters read with the rebuilt key: Relation XXII 634 of 716 (88.5%) + letter of 20 Nov. 1715 741 of 922 (80.4%) = 1,375 of 1,638 = 83.9%. Strict rule after the claims review of 12 Nov 2026: a word counts only if the contributor read it and every letter of it as read is given by the gloss value of the number under it (key c, K1715, or a value a gloss attests: 4 = x, 76 = st, 20 = b, 306 = Vienne from the 1715 glosses, 78 = le from view 0057, 103 = le from view 0080); spelling equivalences u/v, i/j/y, single/double consonant, est/ét, à + le roy = au Roy only. Before the review the script dropped a word only when a number under it had no gloss value (664, 841, 1,505 = 91.9%). The contributor's own counts, under two different rules, were 89.5% and 96.75%.

system.notes: One key in both volumes: key c (glosses of Loc. 00713/01) and K1715 (glosses of Loc. 00712/05) agree on 43 of their 47 common numbers by the verifier's comparison (the contributor counted 47 of 50), share 150, 168 and 700, and each reads the other volume's letter (verification, 12 Nov 2026). The four that differ: 20 (ee / b; b is right), 71 (y / i; the training glosses have y in all 8 cases, so s15_key.tsv's 'i' is a slip), 77 (ss / s), 97 (m / la). Key c's 103 = 'les' reads 'le' in Relation XXII ('le comte de Sinzendorf'). S1 is not the Flemming key K0 (Loc. 00675/10, view 0080), nor its shifted variant, nor Wackerbarth's 1703 key (contributor's comparison). The volume's Nov.-Dec. 1717 letters use another key (S2 = K0); they are outside this entry. By the contributor's report of A.-S. Rous's paper (not opened here), she describes the 1717 system as substitution in 1-3 digit numbers, mostly 2, with 355 and 1000 in the nomenclator.
